superordinate.label: Prevent contamination to reduce washing demand
superordinate.description: Decrease frequency and intensity of laundering by inhibiting attachment and retention of liquids and soils on garments so stains and spills do not require water-intensive cleaning.

basic.label: Surface modification to impart repellency
basic.description: Change fabric surface structure and chemistry to produce durable repellency (superhydrophobicity/self‑cleaning) so contaminants bead, roll off, or fail to adhere.

labels.name: Biocompatible safety formulation
labels.description: Constraining chemical choices to non-toxic, biodegradable ingredients to allow operation without heavy rinsing.

subordinate.label: Nanostructured superhydrophobic coatings / finishes
subordinate.description: Concrete implementations: nanostructured coatings applied as detergents or fabric finishes (e.g., fluorinated polymers, silicones, sol‑gel silica, nanoparticle composites); application methods such as wash‑in finishes, spray or dip coating, or deposition techniques; performance parameters like hierarchical micro/nano roughness, contact angle >150°, low sliding angle, and wash‑durability additives.

idea: Develop laundry detergents or fabric finishes that apply a nanostructured, superhydrophobic coating to clothes. This makes garments inherently resistant to stains and dirt adhesion, causing spills to bead up and roll off, thus requiring less frequent and less intensive washing with water.

superordinate.label: Non‑aqueous, phase‑change cleaning medium
superordinate.description: Replace water with a solvent whose phase behavior and solvency remove soils while reducing water consumption.

superordinate.label: Closed‑loop resource circulation
superordinate.description: Avoid consumptive loss by capturing, purifying, and reusing the cleaning medium within a contained cycle.

superordinate.label: Phase‑transition driven separation
superordinate.description: Exploit pressure/temperature induced phase changes to separate contaminants from the solvent for recovery.

superordinate.label: Pressure‑rated containment and handling
superordinate.description: Provide a sealed, mechanically controlled environment to apply and control solvent conditions safely to garments.

basic.label: Supercritical CO2 as the cleaning solvent
basic.description: Use CO2 at supercritical conditions to solvate oils/soils and act as the primary cleaning agent instead of water.

labels.name: Supercritical fluid cleaning

basic.label: Solvent recovery and recycle subsystem

labels.name: Immediate fluid reclamation
labels.description: Capturing used vapor or condensate, purifying it locally, and recirculating it directly back into the process.

labels.name: Carrier regeneration
labels.description: Processes designed to separate collected contaminants from the transport medium to prepare the carrier for reuse.

basic.label: Pressure/temperature cycling for separation
basic.description: Controlled depressurization/pressurization (or temperature control) to change solvent phase and concentrate/collect contaminants.

labels.name: Sublimation-based soil lift
labels.description: Leveraging the rapid phase change of a solid (e.g., CO2) to gas to physically expand and separate soils from fibers.

labels.name: Thermal contaminant desorption

basic.label: Sealed high‑pressure process chamber with agitation and safety

labels.name: Controlled environment enclosure

subordinate.label: Pressurized CO2 at supercritical conditions (~31°C, 73.8 bar) in sealed drum

subordinate.label: Compressors, condensers/adsorbers, storage vessels, filters
subordinate.description: Concrete components: gas compressors, cold traps or adsorbers to remove collected soils, storage tanks, valves and piping for closed‑loop CO2 handling.

subordinate.label: Controlled depressurization valves and separators

subordinate.label: Pressure‑rated stainless drum, seals, agitator, sensors, safety interlocks
subordinate.description: Materials and hardware: ASME‑rated vessel, high‑pressure seals, mechanical or fluid agitation, pressure/temperature sensors and automatic safety cutoffs.

idea: A home appliance that uses recycled supercritical CO2 as the primary cleaning agent. Clothes are placed in a sealed chamber, CO2 is pressurized to its supercritical state, dissolves dirt, then is depressurized back to a gas for collection and reuse.

superordinate.label: Energy-focused cleaning replacing bulk immersion
superordinate.description: Use concentrated energetic inputs to break adhesion of soils rather than relying on large volumes of water to solubilize and mechanically abrade soils.

superordinate.label: Minimized liquid exposure to textiles
superordinate.description: Limit the amount of liquid contacting fabrics by delivering or retaining only small, controlled liquid volumes where cleaning is needed.

superordinate.label: Containment and fluid management to avoid bulk submersion

superordinate.label: Amplify cleaning chemistry efficiency in low volumes
superordinate.description: Rely on more potent or tailored chemistries so that smaller liquid doses achieve required soil removal when paired with other mechanisms.

basic.description: Generate cavitation in small liquid volumes adjacent to textiles using ultrasound to detach soils via micro-jetting and shock from bubble collapse instead of bulk mechanical friction.

labels.name: Ultrasonic cavitation
labels.description: Using ultrasound to drive oscillating micro-bubbles in a thin liquid film, creating localized forces that dislodge contaminants.

basic.label: Targeted low-volume liquid delivery
basic.description: Apply metered droplets, mists, or thin films of water/solution directly to textiles to provide the minimal medium required for energy-driven cleaning.

labels.name: Low-volume localized rinsing

labels.name: Atomized mist application

basic.label: Drum/containment design for limited fluid contact
basic.description: Geometry, barriers, or internal features that keep textiles out of bulk liquid and create pockets or channels where limited fluid and energy interact with fabric.

labels.name: Fluid-minimizing containment
labels.description: Designing geometries that restrict fluid contact to specific pockets or channels, preventing full immersion.

basic.label: Concentrated, cavitation-compatible cleaning chemistry
basic.description: Formulations (enzymes, surfactants, solvents) optimized to be effective in small liquid volumes and to synergize with cavitation-driven removal.

labels.name: Biocompatible safety formulation

subordinate.label: Misting/spray micro-dosing system

subordinate.description: Examples: drums with sealed pockets or membranes, perforations and channels that prevent pooling, hydrophobic coatings to maintain thin films, and rotational mechanics to refresh fluid layers.

subordinate.label: Concentrate cartridges and low-foaming formulations
subordinate.description: Examples: enzyme- or solvent-rich concentrate cartridges, low-foaming surfactants stable under cavitation, and dosing modules sized for low-volume baths.

idea: Design a washing machine drum where clothes are exposed to a minimal amount of water (or a specialized cleaning solution), which is then agitated by powerful ultrasonic transducers. This intense cavitation provides deep cleaning with significantly less water and mechanical friction than traditional methods.

superordinate.label: Closed-loop low-water cleaning via localized humidification and recovery
superordinate.description: Reduce overall water use by applying minimal, targeted moisture to garments to mobilize soils and then recovering that moisture and captured contaminants within a sealed system for removal and reuse.

basic.label: Mist-based humidification with condensation recovery and filtration
basic.description: Core functional process: generate a fine mist to loosen and lift dirt from fabrics, then condense and collect the resulting moisture (carrying loosened particles) and filter it so water and contaminants are separated and water is recycled or disposed efficiently.

labels.name: Aerosol condensation extraction
labels.description: Generating mist to wet contaminants, followed by condensation and collection to remove the soiled liquid phase.

labels.name: Immediate fluid reclamation
labels.description: Capturing used vapor or condensate, purifying it locally, and recirculating it directly back into the process.

subordinate.label: Sealed cabinet with atomizer, condenser, reservoir, and filters
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation: a closed laundry cabinet containing a fine atomizing mist generator (e.g., ultrasonic or nozzle), dosing of eco‑friendly cleaning agent, cooled condensation surfaces or condenser coils, a collection tank and particulate/chemical filters to capture contaminants and enable low-water-per-cycle operation.

idea: A sealed laundry cabinet that cleans and refreshes clothes using a fine mist of water combined with eco-friendly cleaning agents. The mist humidifies and helps release dirt particles, which are then condensed, collected, and filtered, effectively cleaning with very low water usage per cycle.

superordinate.label: Substitute bulk aqueous washing with non‑liquid surface decontamination
superordinate.description: Reduce the need for full water-based laundering by neutralizing odors and sanitizing fabrics through a non‑aqueous, surface‑focused treatment that restores wearable condition without immersion.

basic.label: Cold plasma exposure to generate reactive species for chemical and biological neutralization
basic.description: Create and apply low‑temperature ionized gas (cold plasma) that produces reactive oxygen/nitrogen species and energetic particles which oxidize/decompose odor‑causing organic compounds and inactivate microbes on textiles.

labels.name: Reactive species oxidation
labels.description: Generating reactive species (plasma, ozone) to chemically oxidize VOCs, odors, and organic soils at the textile interface.

subordinate.label: Appliance‑integrated cold plasma generator and operational parameters
subordinate.description: Concrete implementations and parameters: integrate a cold plasma module into a washing appliance or dedicated garment cabinet; use dielectric barrier discharge, plasma jets, or corona sources; operate at low temperatures safe for fabrics; produce reactive O/N species; define exposure cycles, airflow/filtration, containment and safety interlocks; specify power/HV supply, electrode geometry, and material compatibility testing.

idea: Integrate a cold plasma generator into a laundry appliance or a dedicated garment cabinet. Clothes are exposed to plasma, which effectively breaks down odor-causing compounds and sanitizes the fabric, extending wear time between full washes and significantly reducing water consumption.

superordinate.label: Replace whole-item washing with targeted remediation
superordinate.description: Avoid water-intensive full-garment wash cycles by detecting problem areas and intervening only at those spots.

superordinate.label: In-situ automated cleaning embedded in storage
superordinate.description: Bring detection and remediation to the point of storage (hamper/closet) to eliminate transport and batch processing.

superordinate.label: Minimize resource use via micro-dosing and local mechanical action
superordinate.description: Reduce water and chemical consumption by applying minimal amounts of cleaning agents or local mechanical cleaning only where needed.

subordinate.label: Optical stain detection + decision software
subordinate.description: Vision system (cameras/lighting) combined with on-device image analysis or ML models that localize stains and trigger spot-clean commands to actuators.

subordinate.label: Hamper/closet-mounted robotic module
subordinate.description: Physical implementation: compact robotic arm or articulating head, mounting hardware for storage, power supply, basic navigation/positioning, and scheduling/connectivity.

subordinate.label: Micro-applicators and dry micro-brush heads
subordinate.description: Concrete tools: precision micro-spray valves or pumps for micro-dosing cleaners, sealed small-volume reservoirs, and dry micro-brush or abrasive head assemblies for localized mechanical cleaning.

idea: A smart robotic system, integrated into a laundry hamper or closet, that uses optical sensors to detect stains and dirt. It then applies a micro-dose of targeted cleaning solution or uses a dry micro-brush to remove localized grime, minimizing the need for full-garment, water-intensive washing.

superordinate.label: Reduce water-based laundering demand
superordinate.description: Lower overall household or garment-level water consumption by decreasing the frequency of full wet-wash cycles through alternative, non-aqueous refresh treatments.

superordinate.label: Safe, localized non-liquid treatment
superordinate.description: Provide a controlled environment to apply non-water treatments to textiles while managing safety risks and byproducts so treatments can substitute for washing.

superordinate.label: Targeted substitution for specific garment needs
superordinate.description: Choose and modulate refresh actions so that delicate items, outerwear, or lightly used garments receive limited treatment instead of a full wash.

labels.name: Adaptive process control

subordinate.label: UV-C source and dosage control
subordinate.description: Specific implementation using UV-C (e.g., 254 nm low-pressure lamps or UV-C LEDs) with specified irradiance, timed dosing/pulsing, reflective interior geometry for uniform exposure, and dose monitoring to achieve microbial inactivation and odor molecule degradation.

subordinate.label: Sealed cabinet hardware and safety features
subordinate.description: Concrete chamber elements such as a lockable door with interlocks, reflective lining, hangers/racks, controlled airflow, ozone scavengers or activated-carbon filters, and materials selected to resist UV exposure.

subordinate.label: Sensors, presets, and user interface
subordinate.description: Practical controls and sensors: timers, fabric/weight or humidity/VOC sensors, garment-type presets (delicate/outerwear), smartphone connectivity, and algorithms that recommend or automatically run refresh cycles instead of full laundering.

idea: A garment "freshener" chamber that uses UV-C light to sanitize and deodorize clothes, especially those that are not visibly dirty but need refreshing. This significantly reduces the frequency of water-intensive washes, particularly for delicate items or outerwear.

superordinate.label: Non-liquid force–based contaminant removal
superordinate.description: Remove soil from textiles by applying non-fluid physical forces rather than solvent action.

superordinate.label: Environmental modulation to enable charge processes
superordinate.description: Alter the drum atmosphere (e.g., reduce humidity) to improve generation and retention of electrostatic charge.

superordinate.label: Mechanical exposure of particles
superordinate.description: Use motion to detach and present particles from fabric surfaces so they can be separated.

basic.label: Electrostatic particle separation
basic.description: Generate opposite electric charges on fabric and particulates and remove particulates by attracting them to an oppositely charged collector.

labels.name: Electrohydrodynamic air movement
labels.description: Generating airflow through electric fields (ion wind) to induce non-mechanical air movement for transport or shear.

basic.label: Humidity control to facilitate charging
basic.description: Create and maintain low-moisture conditions that increase charge generation and reduce charge dissipation on materials and particles.

labels.name: Electrostatic charge optimization
labels.description: Controlling humidity/surface conditions to maximize charge generation for particle attraction while managing dissipation.

basic.label: Tumble-induced particle mobilization
basic.description: Use drum rotation and impacts to dislodge, expose, and move particles so they can be charged and captured.

labels.name: Kinematic energy coupling
labels.description: Designing the mechanical interface to transmit tumbling motion into fabric strain or actuator energy efficiently.

subordinate.label: Oppositely charged collector plate or filter in drum
subordinate.description: A metallic or coated plate/filter positioned inside the drum and held at opposite polarity (or connected to a charge-collection medium) to capture charged dirt particles.

subordinate.label: Low-humidity drum implementations
subordinate.description: Concrete methods such as sealed drum with desiccant cartridges, built-in dehumidifier/dry-air inlet, or moisture barriers to achieve reduced relative humidity during the cycle.

subordinate.label: Drum motion and geometry parameters
subordinate.description: Specific tumble parameters (rotation speed, drum baffles/geometry, cycle duration, impact patterns) chosen to maximize particle detachment and exposure.

idea: Design a laundry drum that tumbles clothes in a low-humidity environment, inducing an electrostatic charge on both fabric and dirt particles. The charged dirt particles are then attracted to an oppositely charged collector plate or filter within the drum, effectively "lifting" them off the fabric without water.

superordinate.label: On-device closed-loop resource recovery
superordinate.description: Embedding resource reclamation and reuse within the appliance to eliminate reliance on external supply and reduce discharge.

subordinate.description: Concrete treatment technologies implemented in series: particulate removal (microfiltration), solute removal (reverse osmosis) and disinfection (UV) to achieve near-pristine water.

subordinate.description: Specific sensors (e.g., TDS meter, turbidity probe) and embedded logic that decide whether treated water meets reuse thresholds and adjust treatment or flag discharge.

idea: A washing machine with an integrated, ultra-efficient closed-loop water purification system. After each wash cycle, the greywater undergoes micro-filtration, reverse osmosis, and UV sterilization, making it pristine and immediately reusable for the next load, virtually eliminating water discharge and demand.

superordinate.label: Targeted, low‑resource refresh treatment
superordinate.description: Selective short-duration treatments tuned to material sensitivity and degree of soiling to reduce overall resource use.

labels.name: Thermoelastic shock disruption
labels.description: Inducing rapid thermal expansion/contraction to generate micro-scale shockwaves that break adhesive bonds between soil and fiber.

subordinate.description: Concrete removal method: wiping with a damp cloth after dwell or blotting with a dry absorbent pad to capture solubilized stain fragments without rinsing.

idea: A targeted spray or applicator pen that dispenses a concentrated blend of fabric-safe enzymes onto specific stains. superordinate.label: Dry air-based removal of contaminants to preserve garments

basic.label: Closed-loop air circulation with adsorption/filtration

idea: A sealed garment cabinet where clothes are hung. superordinate.label: Enclosed controlled exposure for targeted treatment

basic.label: Reactive species-driven surface oxidation (non-contact, dry sanitization)

labels.name: Reactive species oxidation

basic.label: Controlled exposure environment (cabinetized appliance)

idea: A garment refreshing cabinet equipped with a DBD plasma generator. Clothes are exposed to the ozone and reactive oxygen/nitrogen species produced by the DBD. superordinate.label: Active electrostatic/electrochemical removal of contaminants

basic.label: Ion‑exchange membrane separation

labels.name: Membrane fluid purification

basic.label: Low-volume suspension and closed-loop recirculation

labels.name: Immediate fluid reclamation

idea: A specialized washing unit where clothes are suspended in a minimal amount of slightly conductive water or a weak electrolyte solution. superordinate.label: Active reversible surface actuation

superordinate.label: Localized stimulus-driven, water-minimal processing

superordinate.label: Material integration with substrate structure

superordinate.label: Containment and separation of expelled contaminants

basic.label: Stimulus-responsive polymer actuation to mechanically expel contaminants

labels.name: Actuated micro-disruption

idea: Develop cleaning agents or fabric coatings containing embedded or surface-applied smart polymers. subordinate.description: Low‑speed fans/blowers, flow plenums or ducts, low‑turbulence flow design, HEPA/electrostatic/cyclone filters or collection canisters, recirculation/venting controls, and noise mitigation components.

subordinate.label: Chamber hardware, user interface, and mounts
subordinate.description: Sealed chamber shell and door seals, observation window or sensors, interchangeable hangers/fixtures for garments, vibration/noise isolation mounts, control panel, safety interlocks, and maintenance access to filters and transducers.

idea: A specialized enclosed chamber where garments are suspended and gently agitated by powerful, non-audible ultrasonic standing waves. This contactless "tumbling" and manipulation effectively loosens dry dirt, dust, and lint from the fabric fibers. A gentle filtered airflow simultaneously draws away the dislodged particles into a collection system, providing a dry, contact-free cleaning and refreshing process without any water or mechanical wear on the fabric.

superordinate.label: Use of externally controllable material-state change to perform work
superordinate.description: Employ a medium whose mechanical properties can be rapidly and reversibly altered by an external input to apply forces or confinement to a target (e.g., contaminants on a substrate).

superordinate.label: Mechanically driven contaminant detachment via transient confinement
superordinate.description: Remove soil by temporarily encapsulating or constraining particles and applying mechanical stress to break adhesion to a substrate.

superordinate.label: Closed-loop capture and removal of liberated contaminants
superordinate.description: Collect and separate dislodged contaminants from the working medium and restore the medium for reuse without replacing the bulk solvent.

superordinate.label: Minimization of working-medium volume and contact duration
superordinate.description: Reduce resource use by limiting the quantity of cleaning medium and the exposure time while maintaining effective interaction with the substrate.

basic.label: Field-controlled, reversible rheology modulation of cleaning medium
basic.description: A working fluid whose viscosity/solid-like behaviour is rapidly switched on and off by an applied field, enabling timed mechanical action without changing composition.

labels.name: Rheology-modulated impact
labels.description: Using fluids that change viscosity under applied fields to deliver tunable mechanical impact forces.

basic.label: Transient encapsulation and mechanical stressing of contaminants
basic.description: Use the medium's transient solidification to surround fibers/particles and apply shear/compressive forces that dislodge oils and dirt.

labels.name: Thin-film peel removal
labels.description: Applying a minimal liquid layer to entrap soil, followed by mechanical removal (wiping/peeling) rather than dilution.

labels.name: Sacrificial film lift-off
labels.description: Applying a temporary film that entraps surface contaminants as it solidifies and removes them when peeled.

basic.label: In-line filtration and purification for medium recycling
basic.description: Separate and remove freed contaminants from the medium and return a purified working fluid to the process, maintaining a closed-loop system.

labels.name: Carrier regeneration

labels.name: Immediate fluid reclamation
labels.description: Capturing used vapor or condensate, purifying it locally, and recirculating it directly back into the process.

basic.label: Low-volume, short-duration immersion protocol
basic.description: Minimize solvent usage by using a small quantity of low-viscosity medium and brief contact periods to limit resource consumption.

labels.name: Stationary, low-volume wash chemistry
labels.description: maintaining non-turbulent, wall-attached airflow to apply persistent, gentle shear forces that detach surface particulates.

labels.name: Fluid-minimizing containment
labels.description: Designing geometries that restrict fluid contact to specific pockets or channels, preventing full immersion.

subordinate.label: Magnetorheological (MR) fluid responsive to pulsed magnetic fields
subordinate.description: A fabric-safe, low-viscosity MR fluid whose particles aggregate under a pulsed magnetic field to thicken around fibers and rapidly thin when the field is removed; implementation details include field strength, pulse timing, and particle chemistry.

subordinate.label: Pulsed magnetic-field protocol for encapsulation and release
subordinate.description: Specific pulse sequences and field gradients that cause momentary thickening around fibers to encapsulate dirt, followed by rapid removal to release loosened contaminants into the bulk medium.

subordinate.label: Continuous filtration and purification modules (microfiltration, coalescers, adsorbents)
subordinate.description: Concrete separation technologies and process parameters: filters, coalescing elements, adsorbents, and recirculation pumps sized to recover contaminants and refresh MR fluid with minimal loss.

subordinate.label: Minimal immersion bath and timed exposure controls
subordinate.description: Design and control details: small-volume bath geometry, conveyor or dip cycles, dwell times, and fluid handling to ensure brief immersion and rapid turnover.

idea: A system where garments are briefly immersed in a minimal volume of a low-viscosity, fabric-safe MR fluid. A pulsed magnetic field is then applied, causing the fluid to momentarily thicken around the fabric fibers, effectively encapsulating and mechanically stressing embedded dirt and oil particles. When the field is removed, the fluid instantly thins, releasing the loosened dirt, which is then carried away by filtration. The fluid is continuously recycled and purified for subsequent uses with minimal loss and no water.

superordinate.label: Localized concentration and retention of contaminants to enable low-water cleaning
superordinate.description: Reduce overall water use by mobilizing contaminants from textiles into a dedicated, reusable interface that preferentially attracts and holds soils, so only a small amount of water is needed to drive transfer and capture.

basic.label: Superhydrophilic wicking capture medium
basic.description: A material interface that preferentially draws in water and dissolved/particulate contaminants from nearby textiles and retains them via capillary/adsorptive mechanisms.

labels.name: Capillary-driven absorption
labels.description: Using porous, hydrophilic materials to draw moisture, dissolved oils, and soils out of textile fibers via capillary action.

basic.label: Minimal-moisture mobilization
basic.description: Use of a very small, fine application of water to solubilize or loosen oils and particulates so they can be transferred to the capture medium without bulk washing.

labels.name: Atomized mist application
labels.description: Delivering cleaning agents via fine mist to solubilize soils with minimal fluid volume.

labels.name: Low-volume localized rinsing
labels.description: Using focused, low-flow fluid application to carry away detached material with minimal water usage.

basic.label: Mechanical contact-driven transfer
basic.description: Agitation, tumbling, or airflow that brings textile surfaces into repeated contact with the capture medium to encourage transfer of loosened contaminants.

labels.name: Kinematic energy coupling
labels.description: Designing the mechanical interface to transmit tumbling motion into fabric strain or actuator energy efficiently.

labels.name: Dry mechanical grooming
labels.description: Using engineered protrusions to physically lift or scrape dry debris and lint without fluid.

basic.label: Regeneration and reuse of the capture medium
basic.description: A process for removing accumulated contaminants from the medium so it can be returned to service, preserving the low-water, low-material footprint.

labels.name: Carrier regeneration
labels.description: Processes designed to separate collected contaminants from the transport medium to prepare the carrier for reuse.

subordinate.label: Reusable superhydrophilic sheet/pad (finely textured)
subordinate.description: A physically sized sheet or pad made from a superhydrophilic, finely textured material (e.g., hydrophilic-coated textile or nanofiber matrix) designed to be placed with garments to wick and hold oils, dissolved dirt, and particulates.

subordinate.label: Very fine, low-volume mist and brief cycle
subordinate.description: An implementation using an aerosolized micro-mist or vaporizing nozzle that supplies a minimal total water volume over a short cycle to mobilize soils without soaking fabrics.

subordinate.label: Placement in tumbler or refresh cabinet with agitation/airflow
subordinate.description: Practical deployment inside a tumbling dryer or a dedicated refresh cabinet where motion and air movement repeatedly press garments against the sheet to promote contaminant transfer.

subordinate.label: Rinse/regeneration protocol
subordinate.description: Cleaning the sheet by rinsing (manual or machine) with water and optionally mild detergent, followed by drying, to remove captured soils and restore capture capacity for reuse.

idea: A specialized, highly reusable sheet or pad made from a superhydrophilic, finely textured material designed to be placed in a tumbling dryer or a dedicated refresh cabinet with clothes. During a brief cycle with a very fine, minimal mist of water, this sheet actively attracts and captures body oils, dissolved dirt, and fine particulate matter released from the garments. The superhydrophilic material "wicks" and holds these contaminants, effectively cleaning the clothes with minimal water, and the sheet is then rinsed clean for reuse.

superordinate.label: Transient binding-and-transfer of contaminants
superordinate.description: Remove soil and odor from textiles by transferring them into a temporarily applied, removable phase that preferentially binds contaminants rather than using bulk solvent to dissolve or flush them away.

superordinate.label: Controlled release/detachment of the capture phase
superordinate.description: Use an externally triggered, predictable change (chemical, mechanical, or environmental) to convert the capture phase from attached to detachable so it separates from the fabric carrying trapped contaminants.

superordinate.label: Closed-loop removal and material stewardship
superordinate.description: Collect the detached contaminant-bearing medium and route it to processing for safe disposal or regeneration, minimizing fresh water and waste output through recovery and treatment.

basic.label: Temporary adhesive capture medium applied to fabric
basic.description: Introduce a transient, fabric-safe medium with selective affinity for dirt/odor molecules that can be applied uniformly to textiles and hold contaminants without leaving residue.

labels.name: Stimulus-responsive capture
labels.description: Using reversible stimuli (charge, light, temp) to adhere debris to a collector and release it into a waste receptacle.

basic.label: Triggered destabilization to shed the medium
basic.description: A mechanism to alter the medium's state or its adhesion to fibers (e.g., change in chemistry or mechanical agitation) in a controlled manner so the medium releases from the textile intact carrying contaminants.

basic.label: Containment and processing of removed medium
basic.description: Systems and processes that capture the detached medium and treat, regenerate, or dispose of it with low water use and minimal environmental impact, enabling reuse or safe waste handling.

labels.name: Fluid-minimizing containment

subordinate.label: Biodegradable hydrogel 'bio-slime' mist in a controlled chamber
subordinate.description: Implementation of the capture medium as a fine mist of a non-toxic, biodegradable hydrogel-based polymer engineered for slight adhesiveness to dirt/odor molecules, applied within a controlled chamber to ensure uniform coverage and fabric safety.

subordinate.label: pH-trigger, mild vibration, or other staged trigger
subordinate.description: Specific detachment triggers such as a programmed pH shift, ionic change, enzymatic action, mild vibrational shaking, or timed thermal cue that causes the hydrogel to break down or shed from fibers into a collectable form.

subordinate.label: Collection sump and regeneration/disposal workflow
subordinate.description: Concrete collection methods (drains, filters, skimmers) and downstream processing like filtration, biodegradation, chemical neutralization, or regeneration loops that recover reusable components and minimize fresh water usage.

idea: A controlled chamber system that applies a fine, non-toxic, biodegradable, and fabric-safe "bio-slime" (e.g., a hydrogel-based polymer with specific adhesive properties) mist onto clothes. This slime is engineered to be slightly adhesive to dirt and odor molecules. After a short dwell time, a second stage triggers a controlled 'shedding' or breakdown of the slime (e.g., via a pH change or mild vibration), causing it to detach from the fabric, carrying the trapped dirt and odors with it, into a collection system. The slime is then processed for disposal or regeneration, leaving clean, residue-free clothes with minimal water usage.

superordinate.label: Dry, targeted chemical transformation of surface contaminants
superordinate.description: Remove organic soils and odors by converting them chemically into removable forms without bulk liquid solvents.

superordinate.label: Active removal of reaction products from the fabric environment
superordinate.description: Physically extract volatile decomposition products and particulates generated by the treatment so they do not redeposit on textiles.

superordinate.label: Material-preserving decontamination
superordinate.description: Achieve cleaning while avoiding thermal, mechanical, or chemical damage to fibers to extend garment life.

superordinate.label: Water- and solvent-minimizing cleaning paradigm
superordinate.description: Replace traditional aqueous or solvent-based cleaning by using alternate reaction media and processes to reduce water and harsh chemical use.

superordinate.label: Controlled exposure environment for uniform treatment
superordinate.description: Use an engineered chamber and delivery geometry to ensure consistent interaction between the reactive agents and all garment surfaces.

basic.label: Plasma-generated reactive species for surface chemical decomposition
basic.description: Create energetic, chemically reactive species (radicals, ions, excited neutrals) via low-temperature plasma to selectively oxidize/reduce and fragment surface organics into volatile products.

labels.name: Reactive species oxidation
labels.description: Generating reactive species (plasma, ozone) to chemically oxidize VOCs, odors, and organic soils at the textile interface.

basic.label: Vacuum/airflow extraction of volatiles and particulates
basic.description: maintain reduced pressure or directed flow to remove volatile byproducts and dislodged particles from the chamber before redeposition.

labels.name: Negative-pressure vapor extraction
labels.description: maintaining reduced pressure to continuously draw volatile byproducts and contaminants away from the fabric to prevent redeposition.

basic.label: Tuning of energy, chemistry, and exposure to protect fibers
basic.description: Control plasma energy, reactive species concentration, exposure duration, and thermal load to achieve effective cleaning without degrading textile materials.

labels.name: Adaptive process control
labels.description: Systems that detect fabric/soil properties and adjust energy inputs to optimize cleaning while preventing damage.

basic.label: Dry-process replacement of aqueous/solvent cleaning
basic.description: Implement a non-liquid cleaning route that accomplishes similar or better removal of common contaminants while minimizing water and chemical use.

labels.name: Controlled environment enclosure
labels.description: A sealed chamber that regulates atmosphere, pressure, and temperature to optimize reaction conditions while containing fluids.

labels.name: Reactive species oxidation

basic.label: Engineered chamber and delivery systems for uniform plasma exposure
basic.description: Provide hardware and fluid/electromagnetic design to distribute reactive species evenly and hold garments in reproducible orientations.

labels.name: Controlled environment enclosure
labels.description: A sealed chamber that regulates atmosphere, pressure, and temperature to optimize reaction conditions while containing fluids.

labels.name: Aerodynamic suspension
labels.description: Supporting textiles using a regulated air cushion to eliminate contact friction and ensure uniform surface exposure.

subordinate.label: Low-temperature oxygen/hydrogen-derived plasma producing radicals and ions
subordinate.description: Specific implementation: cold plasma generated from O2, H2, or precursor gases (e.g., H2O vapor, O2 mixtures) using RF/CCP or other sources to produce radicals (O•, OH•, H•), ions, and metastables that oxidize/reduce surface organics into small volatile molecules.

subordinate.label: Sealed chamber vacuum pumping and controlled flow channels
subordinate.description: Sealed treatment chamber with vacuum pumps and designed airflow ports/filtration to evacuate volatiles and capture particulates without introducing contaminants.

subordinate.label: Parameter set: low power, limited exposure time, gas composition control, and temperature limits
subordinate.description: Concrete parameters and controls: low plasma power density, monitored exposure cycles, tailored gas ratios, and temperature/UV limits chosen to preserve common fabric fibers.

subordinate.label: Dry cleaning workflow replacing wash cycles
subordinate.description: Operational instantiation: a refresh cycle performed in minutes inside a chamber using plasma+vacuum instead of wash/rinse/spin cycles and solvent baths.

subordinate.label: Garment holders, electrode/antenna placement, and flow design
subordinate.description: Physical hardware examples: rotating racks or hangers, distributed electrodes or antennas for homogeneous plasma, and directed flow paths to ensure even exposure and extraction.

idea: A garment refresh chamber where clothes are exposed to a specific low-temperature plasma (e.g., derived from oxygen or hydrogen precursor gases). This plasma generates energetic reactive species tuned to gently react with and break down organic residues (body oils, odors, superficial grime) on the fabric surface. These contaminants are converted into volatile byproducts that are then vacuumed away, providing a deep, dry clean at a molecular level without water or harsh chemicals, thereby extending garment life.

superordinate.label: Directed non-contact forces for particle extraction
superordinate.description: Use of externally generated force fields to mobilize and separate particulate contaminants from a substrate without mechanically agitating the substrate.

superordinate.label: Minimized solvent volume with closed-loop reuse
superordinate.description: Operate cleaning chemistry in a very small solvent volume and retain/recirculate the solvent to reduce fresh solvent input.

superordinate.label: Localized concentration and removal of contaminants
superordinate.description: Collect and concentrate displaced contaminants into a designated capture zone to enable efficient extraction from the solvent.

basic.label: Acoustic-radiation-force particle manipulation
basic.description: Generate controlled acoustic pressure fields that exert radiation forces on suspended dirt/particles, moving and aggregating them independently of bulk fluid motion or garment movement.

labels.name: Acoustic radiation force
labels.description: Using acoustic pressure fields to move or aggregate suspended particles independently of bulk flow.

basic.label: Stationary, low-volume wash chemistry
basic.description: maintain garments immersed in a small-volume solvent with low-concentration cleaning agents and minimal or no induced bulk flow, relying on particle-level removal rather than agitation.

basic.label: Directed capture/filtration of aggregated particulates
basic.description: Provide a localized sink or filter that receives acoustically-aggregated particles, enabling separation of contaminants from the solvent and facilitating solvent reuse.

labels.name: Carrier regeneration
labels.description: Processes designed to separate collected contaminants from the transport medium to prepare the carrier for reuse.

labels.name: Membrane fluid purification
labels.description: Using semi-permeable membranes to separate water from contaminants and cleaning agents for recovery.

subordinate.label: Arrayed high-frequency acoustic transducers (ultrasonic phased array)
subordinate.description: Implementation using a precisely configured array of high-frequency (ultrasonic) transducers and phased-driving electronics to shape standing/propagating acoustic fields and steer radiation forces to target particles.

subordinate.label: Small immersion bath, low-detergent formulation, no mechanical agitation
subordinate.description: Concrete parameters such as a minimal-volume chamber sized to just cover fabrics, dilute surfactant concentrations, and elimination of drum rotation or pumping for agitation.

subordinate.label: Local filter/trap and recirculation plumbing
subordinate.description: Specific capture mechanisms such as microfiltration membranes, particle traps or coalescing pockets positioned where acoustic fields concentrate debris, plus plumbing for returning cleaned solvent to the bath.

idea: A minimal-water wash system where clothes are immersed in a very small volume of water containing a low concentration of cleaning agents. High-frequency acoustic transducers are precisely arrayed to generate acoustic radiation forces that gently 'push' and aggregate dirt particles within the water towards a specific collection zone or filter, without requiring bulk fluid flow or mechanical agitation of the clothes. This allows for highly efficient dirt removal from the water, enabling near-complete water recirculation and minimal fresh water input for effective cleaning.

superordinate.label: Remove contaminants by phase-change transfer rather than bulk liquid flow
superordinate.description: Achieve cleaning by converting a wet, dirt-bearing medium into a solid and then into vapor so contaminants are transported away without relying on liquid drainage or large volumes of water.

superordinate.label: Protect fabric by minimizing wet contact and mechanical stress
superordinate.description: Avoid fabric damage and water retention by limiting the amount and mechanical action of liquid involved in cleaning, relying instead on surface-level, low-impact interactions.

basic.label: Freeze–sublimation based extraction of contaminants
basic.description: A process chain where a minimal cleaning solution wets and encapsulates dirt, the wetted region is frozen to immobilize contaminants, and under reduced pressure the ice/solids sublimate carrying contaminants away as vapor, effecting removal without bulk liquid flow.

labels.name: Freeze-sublimation extraction
labels.description: Freezing wetted soils and removing them via sublimation (lyophilization) under vacuum, bypassing liquid-phase removal.

labels.name: Sublimation-based soil lift
labels.description: Leveraging the rapid phase change of a solid (e.g., CO2) to gas to physically expand and separate soils from fibers.

basic.label: Minimal-wetting, non-mechanical cleaning interface
basic.description: Limit wetting to surface-level coverage (e.g., fine mist), use chemical encapsulation or solubilization at very low liquid volumes, and avoid agitation or centrifugal drainage to reduce fabric stress and water usage.

labels.name: Atomized mist application
labels.description: Delivering cleaning agents via fine mist to solubilize soils with minimal fluid volume.

labels.name: Fluid-minimizing containment
labels.description: Designing geometries that restrict fluid contact to specific pockets or channels, preventing full immersion.

subordinate.label: Concrete freeze–sublimation implementation
subordinate.description: Fine mist application of water plus cleaning agent to lightly wet fibers; freezing by chilled air or cryogenic contact; placement in a low-pressure (vacuum) chamber to sublimate ice/solids; vapor handling and capture of removed contaminants. Parameters include droplet size, freeze temperature, chamber pressure and dwell time.

subordinate.label: Concrete minimal-wetting and low-mechanical implementations
subordinate.description: Misting/nozzle specifications, surfactant or solvent composition formulated for dust encapsulation at low volumes, control of liquid volume per garment (e.g., grams per kg), gentle handling protocols (no tumbling or low-speed cycles), and use of chilled airflow for freezing rather than mechanical contact.

idea: Garments are exposed to a minimal, fine mist of water and a cleaning agent, just enough to lightly wet the fabric and encapsulate dirt. The wetted garment is then gently frozen (e.g., with chilled air) and placed in a low-pressure chamber. The frozen cleaning solution and dirt sublimate away, removing contaminants directly from the fabric structure without liquid drainage or mechanical stress, resulting in clean, dry clothes with minimal water usage.

superordinate.label: Dry mechanical removal of surface contaminants
superordinate.description: Remove particulates and superficial grime from textile fibers using direct mechanical interactions rather than liquid-based chemical or solvent processes.

superordinate.label: Active transport and containment of dislodged material
superordinate.description: Capture and contain particles removed from textiles through controlled airflow and collection, preventing re-deposition and eliminating the need for water-based rinsing.

superordinate.label: Create relative motion to enable fiber-level cleaning
superordinate.description: Use controlled movement between cleaning elements and fabric (tumbling, passing, or moving pads) to expose fibers and enable effective contact-based removal of debris.

basic.label: Micro-scale grooming structures that dislodge particles
basic.description: Use finely engineered, fabric-safe protrusions (bristles, combs, scraping edges) that interact at the scale of fibers to mechanically lift, comb out, or scrape away dry dust, lint, hair, and surface grime.

labels.name: Dry mechanical grooming
labels.description: Using engineered protrusions to physically lift or scrape dry debris and lint without fluid.

basic.label: Integrated suction-based collection
basic.description: Apply directed airflow and suction to remove and transport dislodged particles from the cleaning zone into a containment/filtering subsystem.

labels.name: Controlled low-intensity airflow for particle transport and capture

basic.label: Mechanical agitation via relative motion
basic.description: Generate controlled relative motion (rotation, oscillation, or translation) between fabric and grooming structures to produce repeated contact and shear that loosens debris.

labels.name: Dry mechanical grooming

subordinate.label: Rotating drum or pad arrays with engineered micro-bristles/combs
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation: a rotating drum or a sequence of contact pads fitted with fabric-safe micro-bristles, comb teeth, and small scraping edges inspired by insect grooming geometries; specific materials, bristle stiffness, spacing, tip shape, and mounting density tuned to different fabrics.

subordinate.label: Integrated vacuum channels, dust bin and filtration
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation: built-in vacuum motor and airflow channels adjacent to cleaning surfaces, a removable dust collection chamber, multi-stage filters (e.g., prefilter + HEPA), and valves/ducting designed to capture lint, hair and fine dust without water.

subordinate.label: Tumbling/through-pass motion and speed/force parameters
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation: drum rotation rates, pad reciprocation or conveyor speed, duty cycles, and contact pressure settings (e.g., gentle tumble vs. more aggressive shear) that determine exposure time and mechanical interaction intensity with fabrics.

idea: Design a laundry appliance with a rotating drum or series of pads equipped with precisely engineered, fabric-safe micro-bristles and combs, mimicking insect grooming structures. As clothes tumble or pass through, these structures gently brush, comb, and scrape away dry dust, lint, pet hair, and superficial grime from fabric fibers, collecting them in an integrated vacuum system, thus cleaning without water.

superordinate.label: Enable closed-loop process water reuse
superordinate.description: Reduce reliance on fresh water by capturing, purifying, and immediately returning process water to the washing cycle.

superordinate.label: Selective phase-change separation of water from contaminants
superordinate.description: Use a phase-change barrier that transmits water vapor but rejects dissolved and suspended contaminants to produce high-purity water.

superordinate.label: Lower treatment load via minimal initial use
superordinate.description: Limit the volume and contamination of generated greywater through an intentionally low-water initial wash step.

superordinate.label: Concentrate and isolate contaminants for disposal
superordinate.description: Collect and concentrate rejected solutes/particles into a brine stream that is retained and removed separately from the recovered water.

basic.label: Immediate reuse loop of purified condensate
basic.description: Condense recovered vapor and route the purified condensate directly back into the wash cycle to minimize make-up water demand.

basic.label: Pre-treatment via low-water wash
basic.description: Use a deliberately low-volume wash step to remove soils with minimal water, thereby reducing the volume needing energy-intensive purification.

labels.name: Fluid-minimizing containment

basic.label: Brine concentration and retention
basic.description: Accumulate the non-volatile concentrate (brine) from the separation unit for periodic removal or disposal, preventing recontamination of recovered water.

labels.name: Carrier regeneration
labels.description: Processes designed to separate collected contaminants from the transport medium to prepare the carrier for reuse.

subordinate.label: Condensation coil and direct-feed plumbing
subordinate.description: A heat exchanger/condensing surface and piping that returns condensed water directly to the machine’s wash reservoir or pump head for the next cycle.

subordinate.label: Hydrophobic membrane distillation module (e.g., PTFE MD unit)
subordinate.description: A packaged MD unit comprising a hydrophobic microporous membrane (e.g., PTFE), hot-side and cold-side channels, heat source (waste heat or heater), and condenser to produce ultrapure condensate.

subordinate.label: Minimal-water mechanical/spray wash (specified low volume)
subordinate.description: A wash program and hardware delivering a small, controlled water dose (e.g., low-liter spray/agitation) prior to feeding greywater to the MD unit.

subordinate.label: Brine tank and periodic purge protocol
subordinate.description: A concentrated-brine collection tank with a scheduled drain/disposal or reclamation routine to remove accumulated contaminants retained by the MD process.

idea: A washing machine integrated with a membrane distillation unit. After an initial minimal-water wash, the greywater is fed into the membrane distillation system. Water vapor passes through the hydrophobic membrane, leaving all dissolved and suspended contaminants in the concentrated brine. This purified water is then condensed and immediately recycled for the next wash cycle, achieving ultra-high water recovery and significantly reducing fresh water intake.

superordinate.label: Localized, on-product deployment of cleaning function
superordinate.description: Provide cleaning/refresh functionality directly on the garment so maintenance actions occur at the site of soils or odors rather than via whole-item washing.

superordinate.label: Environmentally triggered maintenance
superordinate.description: Use ambient or mild mechanical/environmental conditions as signals to initiate a maintenance action, enabling passive, demand-driven activity without active user dosing.

superordinate.label: Water-minimizing chemical strategy
superordinate.description: Rely on concentrated or alternative chemistries and spot-treatment approaches that achieve cleaning/odor control with little or no bulk water.

basic.label: Integrated releasable reservoirs in textile structure
basic.description: Embedding discrete, storable cleaning/refresh payloads within the fabric (e.g., microcapsules, microreservoirs) that can be released locally to perform cleaning or deodorization.

labels.name: Active-release micro-reservoirs
labels.description: Integrating discrete payload carriers into the textile that release cleaning agents upon triggering.

labels.name: Localized spot-treatment
labels.description: Mechanisms that target specific stained areas, minimizing overall solvent or energy inventory to the required zone.

basic.label: Passive mechanical/humidity trigger mechanism
basic.description: Mechanisms that cause payload release under low-intensity mechanical stress or specific humidity/temperature conditions associated with wearing or gentle refresh cycles.

labels.name: Stimulus-responsive capture
labels.description: Using reversible stimuli (charge, light, temp) to adhere debris to a collector and release it into a waste receptacle.

basic.label: Concentrated, fabric-safe cleaning/odor chemistries
basic.description: Use of concentrated, low-water-demand formulations and odor-neutralizing agents designed to be effective in small, localized doses and compatible with textile materials.

labels.name: Biocompatible safety formulation
labels.description: Constraining chemical choices to non-toxic, biodegradable ingredients to allow operation without heavy rinsing.

subordinate.label: Microcapsules and embedding techniques
subordinate.description: Specific implementations such as polymer microcapsules, core–shell microreservoirs, encapsulation processes (coacervation, spray-drying), integration into fibers/yarns or coatings, release-by-rupture or controlled diffusion.

subordinate.label: Trigger parameters and devices
subordinate.description: Concrete triggers and conditions: gentle tumbling in a refresh cabinet, wearer motion or friction thresholds, elevated humidity or temperature windows, shell fragility specifications, mechanical design of refresh devices.

subordinate.label: Agent types and formulation details
subordinate.description: Examples of agents and formulations: concentrated enzymatic spot cleaners, solvent-free surfactant concentrates, odor absorbers/neutralizers (e.g., cyclodextrins, activated materials), pH-adjusted microdroplets, stabilizers to preserve payload in fabric.

idea: Garments are manufactured with embedded, fabric-safe microcapsules containing a concentrated, low-water cleaning agent or odor neutralizer. When the garment is worn or experiences mild mechanical stress (e.g., gentle tumbling in a refresh cabinet with slight humidity), some capsules burst, releasing their contents to spot-clean, remove odors, or refresh the fabric locally, significantly extending the time between full water washes.

superordinate.label: Selective removal of volatile contaminants
superordinate.description: Achieve cleaning effect by selectively capturing and removing volatile compounds responsible for unwanted odors rather than using bulk solvent or water to extract soils.

superordinate.label: Directed contact via airflow
superordinate.description: Bring airborne contaminants into controlled contact with a treatment medium by moving air through and around textiles.

superordinate.label: Cyclic restoration of treatment capacity
superordinate.description: Restore the capturing ability of the treatment medium through periodic cycles that release concentrated waste for disposal or further processing.

superordinate.label: Non-destructive, material-safe treatment
superordinate.description: Preserve the physical and aesthetic properties of textiles by using chemically and physically gentle mechanisms that avoid immersion or harsh reagents.

basic.label: Regenerable sorbent bed that selectively adsorbs VOCs
basic.description: A solid-phase capture medium engineered to reversibly bind odor-causing volatile organic compounds with high capacity and selectivity; the primary locus where contaminants are removed from the air stream.

labels.name: Volatile chemical sorption
labels.description: Using a gas-phase carrier with a binding agent to selectively sorb dirt/odors from fabric and transport them away.

basic.label: Air circulation and routing system
basic.description: Mechanisms to circulate ambient or recirculated air through garments and then through the sorbent bed to transfer volatile contaminants from textiles to the capture medium.

labels.name: Controlled low-intensity airflow for particle transport and capture

basic.label: Regeneration subsystem (thermal/pressure swing)
basic.description: A controlled process to desorb and concentrate captured volatiles from the sorbent, restoring capture capacity and producing a manageable waste stream for disposal or further treatment.

labels.name: Thermal contaminant desorption
labels.description: Applying controlled heat to drive volatile organics from fibers into the gas phase without solvents.

labels.name: Carrier regeneration
labels.description: Processes designed to separate collected contaminants from the transport medium to prepare the carrier for reuse.

basic.label: Fabric-safe process constraints
basic.description: Operational and material constraints ensuring the treatment does not damage textiles (e.g., limits on temperature, chemical reactivity, mechanical agitation).

labels.name: Adaptive process control
labels.description: Systems that detect fabric/soil properties and adjust energy inputs to optimize cleaning while preventing damage.

subordinate.label: Modified amines, MOFs, or other regenerable sorbent formulations
subordinate.description: Concrete materials and formulations such as functionalized amine sorbents or metal–organic frameworks designed for reversible VOC binding, selected for capacity, selectivity, kinetics, and regenerability.

subordinate.label: Fan-driven closed-loop ducts, flow rates, and garment fixtures
subordinate.description: Specific implementations including fans, baffles, ducting, hangers or racks, and target airflow rates that route contaminated air from garments over the sorbent bed under controlled residence times.

subordinate.label: Resistive heating or vacuum/pressure-swing hardware and cycles
subordinate.description: Concrete regeneration methods such as low-temperature heaters, timed heating profiles, vacuum pumps, valves, and cycle durations/temperatures/pressures used to desorb and concentrate trapped volatiles.

subordinate.label: Low-temperature operation, inert sorbent surfaces, no-solvent protocols
subordinate.description: Specific constraints and choices like maximum allowable temperatures, use of chemically inert sorbent coatings, avoidance of aqueous or solvent baths, and monitoring to prevent fabric exposure to damaging conditions.

idea: A garment refreshing cabinet that utilizes a bed of regenerable, fabric-safe chemical sorbents (e.g., modified amines or Metal-Organic Frameworks). These sorbents are specifically engineered to reversibly bind volatile organic compounds (VOCs) responsible for odors. Air is circulated through the garments and then over the sorbent bed, trapping odors. The sorbent is then periodically regenerated (e.g., by heating or pressure swing), releasing concentrated odors for safe disposal, making this a highly efficient, water-free, and chemical-free deodorization system.

superordinate.label: Active field-driven manipulation for cleaning
superordinate.description: Use of externally applied fields to actively move and agitate cleaning fluid at the site of soil to dislodge contaminants.

superordinate.label: Minimized, localized fluid delivery
superordinate.description: Reduce overall water use by delivering very small amounts of cleaning fluid only to contaminated regions.

superordinate.label: Directed removal and separation of spent fluid
superordinate.description: Collect and separate contaminated cleaning fluid after treatment to prevent re-soiling and enable low-volume disposal or recycling.

basic.label: Electro/field-driven droplet manipulation and agitation
basic.description: Generate dynamic electric (or similar) fields across a substrate to move, oscillate, or shear micro-droplets on fabric, producing mechanical action that dislodges soil.

labels.name: Electrohydrodynamic air movement
labels.description: Generating airflow through electric fields (ion wind) to induce non-mechanical air movement for transport or shear.

labels.name: Actuated micro-disruption
labels.description: Using small-scale actuators (brushes, piezos) to directly agitate fibers or dislodge particles locally.

basic.label: Targeted micro-droplet application of low-volume cleaning agent
basic.description: Precisely deposit micro-droplets of a specialized low-surface-tension cleaning solution onto stained or soiled areas to concentrate chemical action where needed.

labels.name: Localized spot-treatment
labels.description: Mechanisms that target specific stained areas, minimizing overall solvent or energy inventory to the required zone.

labels.name: Fluid-minimizing containment
labels.description: Designing geometries that restrict fluid contact to specific pockets or channels, preventing full immersion.

basic.label: Electrowetting-guided transport and collection of contaminated droplets
basic.description: Use controlled wetting and electric-field-driven routing to gather, move, and evacuate contaminated droplets to a dedicated collection port.

labels.name: Electrowetting transport
labels.description: Manipulating surface wettability via electric fields to guide contaminated droplets to collection points.

subordinate.label: Electrode array under flat/curved support generating dynamic fields
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation: patterned electrodes beneath a garment-support surface that produce time-varying electric fields to translate, oscillate, or shear individual micro-droplets on fabric.

subordinate.label: Precision nozzle array + low-surface-tension cleaning formulation
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation: a matrix of precision nozzles that deposit micro-droplets of a formulated low-surface-tension cleaning solution onto targeted stain locations on a flat/slightly curved laying surface.

subordinate.label: Electrowetting channels and collection port
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation: electrowetting-controlled pathways and a collection reservoir/port that guide and capture dirty droplets for removal with minimal residual fluid.

idea: A flat or slightly curved surface where garments are laid. A system of precise nozzles applies micro-droplets of a specialized, low-surface-tension cleaning solution to stained areas. Electrodes beneath the surface then apply electric fields to dynamically move, oscillate, or "scrub" these droplets over the fabric, dislodging dirt. The dirty droplets are then electro-wetting-guided to a collection port, allowing for extremely targeted cleaning with minuscule water usage.

superordinate.label: Mechanically dislodge contaminants from textiles using non-liquid energy
superordinate.description: Use transmitted mechanical energy to break adhesion between particles and fabric fibers, enabling cleaning without solvent or water immersion.

superordinate.label: Transport and capture dislodged particles via airflow and filtration
superordinate.description: Collect and contain loosened debris by directing gentle airflow toward a capture medium so particles are removed from the fabric and not re-deposited.

basic.label: Broadband mechanical-wave agitation (compressional + shear)
basic.description: Produce and couple a broad spectrum of mechanical waves, including both compressional and shear components, through the textile to physically agitate fibers and detach varied soils without relying on a single resonance.

labels.name: Acoustic radiation force
labels.description: Using acoustic pressure fields to move or aggregate suspended particles independently of bulk flow.

labels.name: Kinematic energy coupling
labels.description: Designing the mechanical interface to transmit tumbling motion into fabric strain or actuator energy efficiently.

basic.label: Controlled low-intensity airflow for particle transport and capture
basic.description: Use directed, gentle airflow to lift, transport, and convey dislodged particles to a filtration or collection subsystem, minimizing fiber disturbance while enabling dry removal.

labels.name: Controlled low-intensity airflow for particle transport and capture

subordinate.label: Multi-modal transducer array and waveform synthesis
subordinate.description: Concrete implementations: arrays of actuators (e.g., piezoelectric, electromagnetic, ultrasonic) configured to generate broadband drive signals that include compressional and shear modes; fixtures or coupling interfaces to transmit waves into fabric; control electronics for non-resonant waveform shaping.

subordinate.label: Gentle blower/fan, ducts/nozzles, and filtration media
subordinate.description: Concrete implementations: low-pressure fans or blowers, ducting and directional nozzles, particulate filters (mesh, HEPA, cyclonic separators), particle collection trays or cartridges; tunable flow rates and pressure to balance pickup and fabric care.

idea: A garment cleaning chamber equipped with multi-modal transducers capable of generating a broadband spectrum of mechanical waves, including both compressional and shear waves, that propagate through the fabric. These complex vibrations are designed to physically agitate and break the adhesion of diverse dirt particles (dry dust, sticky grime) from fibers across various fabric types. Dislodged particles are then removed by a gentle airflow and filtration system, achieving dry cleaning without specific reliance on a single resonance.

superordinate.label: Suppress microbial odor by modifying storage environment
superordinate.description: Prevent or slow the biological processes that create clothing odors by changing the local environmental conditions around garments (e.g., gas composition, microclimate) rather than cleaning or applying chemicals.

basic.label: maintain a controlled hypoxic microenvironment around garments
basic.description: Create and sustain a low-oxygen atmosphere in the clothing storage volume to directly inhibit metabolic activity and growth of odor-causing microbes; entails containment and active atmosphere regulation as the functional mechanism.

labels.name: Hypoxic biological inhibition
labels.description: maintaining a low-oxygen atmosphere to metabolically stifle the growth of odor-causing microbes.

labels.name: Controlled environment enclosure
labels.description: A sealed chamber that regulates atmosphere, pressure, and temperature to optimize reaction conditions while containing fluids.

subordinate.label: Sealed smart wardrobe with O2 control and sensors
subordinate.description: A garment cabinet that is sealed and equipped with oxygen sensors, gas control (e.g., nitrogen flushing or oxygen scrubbing), valves, control electronics, seals and safety interlocks to lower and hold oxygen concentration at target setpoints around stored clothes.

idea: A smart wardrobe or garment cabinet that maintains a precisely controlled, low-oxygen (hypoxic) internal atmosphere. By reducing the oxygen concentration around garments, the growth and metabolic activity of odor-causing bacteria and fungi are significantly inhibited, effectively preventing the development of unpleasant smells and extending the freshness of clothes without washing or chemical deodorizers, thus reducing water usage.

superordinate.label: Localized energy-enabled soil disruption
superordinate.description: Using a focused external energy source to induce mechanical or chemical effects at fabric surfaces that weaken adhesion of soils without bulk fluid washing.

superordinate.label: Sacrificial particulate-mediated soil engagement
superordinate.description: Introduce and use removable fine particles that contact, abrade, or encapsulate contaminants to enable their removal.

superordinate.label: Contactless removal and recovery of loosened material
superordinate.description: Collect and separate the dislodged soil and spent agents from the fabric in a non-destructive, non-wetting way.

basic.label: Energy–particle mediated mechanical detachment
basic.description: Core process where externally applied energy couples to added particles to produce localized photomechanical action that lifts or etches away dirt from the substrate.

labels.name: Kinematic energy coupling
labels.description: Designing the mechanical interface to transmit tumbling motion into fabric strain or actuator energy efficiently.

labels.name: Micro-abrasive extraction
labels.description: Using fine, benign solid particles to physically abrade or carry soil away via direct contact mechanics.

basic.label: Dry, biodegradable micro-abrasive agent application
basic.description: Applying fine, removable particles that act as transient abrasives or carriers for soil, designed to be benign and separable after use.

labels.name: Micro-abrasive extraction
labels.description: Using fine, benign solid particles to physically abrade or carry soil away via direct contact mechanics.

basic.label: Vacuum-based extraction of particle–soil mixture
basic.description: Suction and filtration system that removes the contaminated particles from the fabric while containing and recovering waste.

labels.name: Thermal-suction extraction
labels.description: Combining localized heating (evaporation) with vacuum extraction to mobilize and remove fluid and soil simultaneously.

labels.name: Carrier regeneration
labels.description: Processes designed to separate collected contaminants from the transport medium to prepare the carrier for reuse.

subordinate.label: Low-power pulsed laser scanning for photomechanical activation
subordinate.description: Implementation using a precisely controlled, low-power pulsed laser beam scanned across fabric to activate micro-abrasive particles and create localized mechanical effects.

subordinate.label: Fine biodegradable cellulose micro-beads dusted onto garments
subordinate.description: Concrete material choice and delivery: very fine, dry, biodegradable micro-abrasive powder (e.g., cellulose beads) gently applied to clothing surfaces.

subordinate.label: Vacuum collection with filters to remove spent particles and soil
subordinate.description: Concrete removal system: vacuuming of the dirty micro-abrasive with containment and filtration for waste handling and possible reuse.

idea: A garment cleaning system where a very fine, dry, and biodegradable micro-abrasive powder (e.g., cellulose beads) is gently dusted onto clothes. A precisely controlled, low-power pulsed laser beam then scans the fabric. The laser energy interacts with the micro-abrasive particles, causing them to gently 'lift' or 'etch' away dirt and grime from the fabric surface through localized photomechanical action. The dirty micro-abrasive is then vacuumed away, providing a contactless, water-free cleaning method.

superordinate.label: Localized electrochemical transformation of contaminants
superordinate.description: Use electric current to drive redox reactions at the fabric surface that break down organic dirt, stains, and odors into simpler compounds.

superordinate.label: Minimized bulk liquids via targeted conductive medium
superordinate.description: Avoid immersing garments by using a thin, localized conductive medium to enable surface reactions without large water volumes.

superordinate.label: Targeted energy delivery to specific areas
superordinate.description: Precisely apply energy and reaction conditions only where needed (spots or small regions) to reduce resource use and avoid whole-garment treatment.

superordinate.label: Convert contaminants to removable forms
superordinate.description: Transform soil and odor molecules into water-soluble or volatile products that can be removed with minimal mechanical action or evaporation.

basic.label: Electrochemical oxidation/degradation at fabric interface
basic.description: Electrochemical reactions (direct electron transfer or mediator-generated reactive species) occur at electrodes interfacing with the fabric, chemically degrading organic contaminants.

labels.name: Reactive species oxidation
labels.description: Generating reactive species (plasma, ozone) to chemically oxidize VOCs, odors, and organic soils at the textile interface.

basic.label: Thin conductive electrolyte film as reaction medium
basic.description: A minimal-volume, slightly conductive, fabric-safe solution forms a film that enables ionic conduction and local electrochemistry on textile surfaces.

labels.name: Fluid-minimizing containment
labels.description: Designing geometries that restrict fluid contact to specific pockets or channels, preventing full immersion.

labels.name: Thin-film peel removal
labels.description: Applying a minimal liquid layer to entrap soil, followed by mechanical removal (wiping/peeling) rather than dilution.

basic.label: Localized electrode delivery system
basic.description: Hardware and electrode geometries that position and control current/voltage at targeted spots—handheld probes or small chambers that confine treatment.

labels.name: Localized spot-treatment
labels.description: Mechanisms that target specific stained areas, minimizing overall solvent or energy inventory to the required zone.

labels.name: Robotic positioning
labels.description: Integrating automated actuators to navigate cleaning tools to specific coordinates for autonomous spot treatment.

basic.label: Post-reaction removal mechanism
basic.description: Methods to remove or disperse degraded products (wiping, blotting, evaporation, mild airflow/heat) so treated residues do not require bulk rinsing.

labels.name: Low-volume localized rinsing
labels.description: Using focused, low-flow fluid application to carry away detached material with minimal water usage.

labels.name: Thermal contaminant desorption
labels.description: Applying controlled heat to drive volatile organics from fibers into the gas phase without solvents.

subordinate.label: Anode-driven oxidation / reactive species generation
subordinate.description: Specific implementations: controlled anode potentials, pulse/current profiles, mediator chemistries or electrode materials that produce hydroxyl radicals, ozone, or direct oxidation pathways to break down organics.

subordinate.label: Fabric-safe slightly conductive solutions and application formats
subordinate.description: Concrete choices: low-volume aqueous electrolyte with benign salts or surfactants applied as spray, pad, droplet, or thin soaked blotter; controlled volume and conductivity parameters.

subordinate.label: Handheld probes or small chamber electrode designs
subordinate.description: Concrete devices: handheld wand with contact electrodes or microelectrode array, miniature chamber with electrode plates, rollers, insulating masks; control electronics for current, pulse, and safety interlocks.

subordinate.label: Wiping, blotting, mild heating or airflow to remove products
subordinate.description: Concrete removal actions: microfiber wiping, absorbent blotting pads, low-heat drying or directed airflow to evaporate volatiles or disperse water-soluble fragments; optional minimal rinsing.

idea: A targeted handheld device or a small chamber with specialized electrodes. Garments, or specific soiled areas, are exposed to a minimal film of a slightly conductive, fabric-safe electrolyte solution. An electric current is then precisely applied, generating reactive species or directly oxidizing organic dirt, stains, and odor molecules on the fabric surface. These contaminants are electrochemically degraded into simpler, water-soluble, or volatile compounds, which are then wiped away or evaporated, minimizing water usage and avoiding harsh chemicals.

superordinate.label: Selective contaminant transfer into a mobile non-aqueous phase
superordinate.description: Extract contaminants from textile substrates by moving them into a controlled, non‑aqueous mobile phase via selective, reversible binding and phase transfer.

superordinate.label: Closed‑loop resource circulation and recovery
superordinate.description: Continuously separate, purify, and recycle process media (carrier and binding agent) to minimize consumption and emissions.

superordinate.label: Controlled exposure environment
superordinate.description: Contain and regulate the interaction between substrate and mobile phase through a sealed, low‑energy treatment environment.

basic.label: Gas‑phase carrier with reversible binding agent (extraction mechanism)
basic.description: A volatile binding agent delivered in a carrier gas vaporizes/diffuses into fabric, selectively sorbs or complexes dirt and odors, then desorbs into the moving gas stream for transport — providing the primary contaminant transfer mechanism.

labels.name: Volatile chemical sorption
labels.description: Using a gas-phase carrier with a binding agent to selectively sorb dirt/odors from fabric and transport them away.

basic.label: Separation, purification, and reuse subsystem
basic.description: Processes and modules that remove captured contaminants from the mobile phase and regenerate both carrier and binding agent for reuse (e.g., capture, separation, and regeneration stages).

labels.name: Carrier regeneration
labels.description: Processes designed to separate collected contaminants from the transport medium to prepare the carrier for reuse.

labels.name: Immediate fluid reclamation
labels.description: Capturing used vapor or condensate, purifying it locally, and recirculating it directly back into the process.

basic.label: Sealed, controlled treatment chamber and flow management
basic.description: A contained apparatus that controls temperature, pressure, gas composition, flow patterns, and exposure time to enable effective gas‑phase extraction while preventing losses and contamination.

labels.name: Controlled environment enclosure
labels.description: A sealed chamber that regulates atmosphere, pressure, and temperature to optimize reaction conditions while containing fluids.
