subordinate.label: Concrete carrier and binding agent choices and operating parameters
subordinate.description: Examples: inert or low‑reactivity carrier gases (N2, CO2, recycled dry air); non‑toxic, fabric‑safe volatile sorbents or ligand vapors (tailored volatile glycols/oligomers or surfactant vapors) formulated to vaporize/diffuse at low temperatures; control parameters such as vapor concentration, flow rate, and exposure time to drive adsorption/desorption.

subordinate.label: Concrete separation and regeneration technologies
subordinate.description: Examples: condensers to recover volatile agent, adsorption beds or chromatographic/molecular‑sieve columns to capture soils, distillation or membrane units to purify agent, and integrated sensors/controllers for continuous regeneration and monitoring.

subordinate.label: Concrete chamber design and controls
subordinate.description: Examples: sealed chamber with garment racks, controlled temperature range (near‑ambient to moderate heat ~up to ~60°C), adjustable flow paths and recirculation valves, seals/filters to contain emissions, and instrumentation for pressure, humidity and gas composition.

idea: A sealed chamber where garments are exposed to a precise, low-temperature, recycled carrier gas containing a non-toxic, fabric-safe binding agent. This agent selectively vaporizes, diffuses into the fabric, adsorbs to dirt and odor molecules, and then is carried away by the gas stream to a separation and recovery unit. The carrier gas and binding agent are continuously purified and reused, effectively "chromatographically eluting" dirt and odors from the fabric without water.

superordinate.label: Selective energy-driven detachment
superordinate.description: Use targeted energy input that is preferentially absorbed by contaminants or their interface to cause their release from the substrate.

superordinate.label: Transient thermo-mechanical conversion
superordinate.description: Convert rapid, localized temperature changes into mechanical impulses at micro-scales to overcome adhesive bonds.

superordinate.label: Contactless capture and removal
superordinate.description: Collect and remove dislodged particles without physical wiping or liquid rinsing using gentle directed flow and filtration.

superordinate.label: Targeted control to protect substrate
superordinate.description: Adjust and guide the energy delivery to affect contaminants while minimizing damage or alteration of the underlying fabric.

basic.label: Localized pulsed energy to produce detachment forces
basic.description: Deliver short, localized energy pulses that are absorbed preferentially by dirt/interface to create forces that detach particles from the fabric.

labels.name: Ion/particle beam sputtering
labels.description: Directing focused beams of ions/particles to impart kinetic energy that ejects contaminants at a molecular level.

labels.name: Localized spot-treatment
labels.description: Mechanisms that target specific stained areas, minimizing overall solvent or energy inventory to the required zone.

basic.label: Thermoelastic shockwave generation
basic.description: Rapid thermal expansion and contraction of the absorbing region generates micro-scale mechanical shockwaves that break adhesive bonds.

labels.name: Thermoelastic shock disruption
labels.description: Inducing rapid thermal expansion/contraction to generate micro-scale shockwaves that break adhesive bonds between soil and fiber.

basic.label: Airflow-based transport and filtration
basic.description: Use low-velocity, directed airflow to carry detached particles to a capture stage where they are filtered and removed from the system.

labels.name: Laminar shear airflow
labels.description: maintaining non-turbulent, wall-attached airflow to apply persistent, gentle shear forces that detach surface particulates.

basic.label: Sensing and selective targeting
basic.description: Scan and tune energy parameters (wavelength, pulse, position) based on material and contaminant properties to maximize selectivity and avoid substrate damage.

labels.name: Adaptive process control
labels.description: Systems that detect fabric/soil properties and adjust energy inputs to optimize cleaning while preventing damage.

labels.name: Optical residue detection
labels.description: Using sensors to identify specific locations of remaining organic residue for targeted cleaning.

subordinate.label: Pulsed infrared laser scanning subsystem
subordinate.description: Low-power pulsed infrared laser (specified wavelength range, pulse energy, spot size) with scanning optics to illuminate contaminant sites; parameters tuned to contaminant absorption.

subordinate.label: Pulse timing and thermal parameters
subordinate.description: Short pulse durations and repetition rates that produce rapid local heating/cooling (thermoelastic regime), spot sizes and energy densities chosen to generate micro-shockwaves without bulk heating.

subordinate.label: Gentle airflow and filtration module
subordinate.description: Low-flow fans or directed nozzles, airflow channels positioned to sweep dislodged particles, and filtration (e.g., HEPA or mechanical filters) to capture debris; may include particle traps and exhaust routing.

subordinate.label: Sensors and control electronics
subordinate.description: Optical/IR cameras or spectrometers, feedback control, scanner actuators, and software that map contaminant locations and adjust laser wavelength/power/scan to protect fabric.

idea: A garment cleaning system where a low-power, pulsed infrared laser scans the fabric. The laser energy is tuned to be preferentially absorbed by dirt particles or the interface layer, causing rapid, localized thermal expansion and contraction. This generates micro-scale mechanical shockwaves that break the adhesive bonds of dirt particles, which are then removed by a gentle airflow and filtration, providing a contactless, water-free cleaning method.

superordinate.label: Transfer-based contaminant extraction
superordinate.description: Remove soils and oils from textiles by transferring them onto a separate, reusable surface rather than dissolving them into bulk water.

superordinate.label: On-board regeneration of the receiving surface
superordinate.description: Sustain extraction performance by continuously restoring the contaminant-receiving surface so it can accept more dirt without manual replacement.

superordinate.label: Controlled mechanical contact for selective transfer
superordinate.description: Use guided, gentle mechanical engagement between textiles and the receiving medium to promote transfer while avoiding fabric damage.

basic.label: Selective, high-affinity contact surfaces
basic.description: Surfaces engineered (chemically and/or physically) to preferentially attract and hold common dirt/oil molecules more strongly than fabric fibers, enabling directional transfer of contaminants.

labels.name: Adhesive contact rolling
labels.description: Using sticky or structured surfaces to physically lift dry particulates and fibers via direct contact adhesion.

basic.label: Continuous surface regeneration subsystem
basic.description: Mechanism(s) that remove collected contaminants from the receiving surface in real time (mechanical, chemical, or combined) and recover or contain the removed soils for reuse or disposal.

labels.name: Carrier regeneration
labels.description: Processes designed to separate collected contaminants from the transport medium to prepare the carrier for reuse.

basic.label: Rotational conveyance and contact control
basic.description: Mechanical arrangement that brings garments into controlled contact with the receiving surfaces (rotation, pressure, speed, and path) to effect transfer without excessive abrasion.

labels.name: Kinematic energy coupling
labels.description: Designing the mechanical interface to transmit tumbling motion into fabric strain or actuator energy efficiently.

subordinate.label: Polymer rollers with tailored surface chemistry/texture
subordinate.description: Cylindrical polymer rollers (specific polymers or coatings) with micro-texture and surface functionalization designed for high oil/dirt affinity versus fabric; parameters include surface energy, roughness, and contact area.

subordinate.label: Integrated scraper and/or micro-solvent spray with recovery
subordinate.description: Concrete regeneration implementations such as a mechanical scraper, wiping element, or low-volume solvent/mist spray combined with a collection and filtration/recycling loop and containment reservoir.

subordinate.label: Motor-driven roller assembly and garment feed controls
subordinate.description: Implementation details including rotating roller shafts, motor and gearing, garment feed/guide path, adjustable nip pressure, and speed/pressure control settings to ensure gentle, consistent contact.

idea: A laundry appliance featuring a series of rotating polymer rollers whose surfaces are engineered to have a higher affinity for common dirt and oil molecules than for fabric fibers. As garments pass through, these rollers gently contact the fabric, transferring dirt and oils from the clothes onto their own surfaces. A secondary, integrated mechanism continuously cleans the rollers (e.g., with a scraper or micro-solvent spray which is then recovered), enabling continuous dirt removal from clothes without water.

superordinate.label: Selective energy-mediated adhesion modification
superordinate.description: Use targeted non-contact energy to change the mechanical or interfacial properties of contaminants or the contaminant–fabric interface so adhesion is reduced without broadly altering the substrate.

superordinate.label: Gentle mechanical detachment
superordinate.description: Apply controlled mechanical forces or fluid flows to separate already-weakened contaminants from the fabric.

superordinate.label: Dry particulate capture and containment
superordinate.description: Collect and retain dislodged particles from the cleaning environment without using liquid solvents.

superordinate.label: Targeted system control and protection
superordinate.description: Continuously monitor and adjust treatment parameters to maximize selectivity for contaminants and prevent damage to the fabric.

basic.label: Electromagnetic-field-induced selective heating/softening
basic.description: Generate tuned RF/microwave fields to induce localized heating or softening in contaminants or the interfacial layer, exploiting dielectric/thermal contrast so the fabric remains largely unaffected.

labels.name: Thermal contaminant desorption
labels.description: Applying controlled heat to drive volatile organics from fibers into the gas phase without solvents.

labels.name: Thermoelastic shock disruption
labels.description: Inducing rapid thermal expansion/contraction to generate micro-scale shockwaves that break adhesive bonds between soil and fiber.

basic.label: Low-intensity agitation or directed airflow
basic.description: Provide controlled tumbling, vibration, or air currents that produce shear/peel forces sufficient to dislodge particles once adhesion is reduced.

labels.name: Laminar shear airflow
labels.description: maintaining non-turbulent, wall-attached airflow to apply persistent, gentle shear forces that detach surface particulates.

labels.name: Actuated micro-disruption
labels.description: Using small-scale actuators (brushes, piezos) to directly agitate fibers or dislodge particles locally.

basic.label: Filtration and particulate separation
basic.description: Remove, separate and retain detached solid particles from the chamber atmosphere to prevent re-deposition and enable disposal or cleaning of collected material.

labels.name: Carrier regeneration
labels.description: Processes designed to separate collected contaminants from the transport medium to prepare the carrier for reuse.

basic.label: Sensing-driven parameter optimization and safety
basic.description: Use sensors and control logic to select frequency, power, exposure patterns and mechanical settings based on contaminant signatures and fabric tolerance, with interlocks to avoid overheating.

labels.name: Adaptive process control
labels.description: Systems that detect fabric/soil properties and adjust energy inputs to optimize cleaning while preventing damage.

subordinate.label: RF/microwave chamber and modulation schemes
subordinate.description: Garment treatment chamber outfitted with RF/microwave emitters, frequency selection and power control (continuous/pulsed), field-shaping antennas, exploitation of dielectric contrast and localized heating protocols to soften/expand soils while limiting fabric temperature.

subordinate.label: Tumbling drums, vibration actuators, and air-jet systems
subordinate.description: Concrete implementations such as slowly rotating drum with padded motion, low-amplitude vibration actuators, directed air jets or controlled laminar flows; specified speeds, amplitudes, and duty cycles matched to fragile fabrics.

subordinate.label: Filter cartridges and separators (HEPA, cyclone, electrostatic)
subordinate.description: Specific capture technologies like removable HEPA-like filter cartridges, cyclone separators, electrostatic precipitators and vacuum-assisted collection boxes; serviceable containment and disposal interfaces.

subordinate.label: Temperature/IR/dielectric/particle sensors and control software
subordinate.description: Sensors (IR, thermistors, dielectric property sensors, particle counters), control algorithms that adjust field frequency/power and mechanical settings, user presets and safety interlocks, and feedback loops for selective treatment.

idea: A garment chamber where clothes are exposed to precisely tuned RF or microwave fields. The frequency and power are optimized to selectively heat and slightly expand/soften the dirt particles or the interface layer between dirt and fabric, without significantly heating the fabric itself. This localized thermal stress, combined with gentle mechanical tumbling or air currents, causes the dirt to lose adhesion and be dislodged. A filtration system then collects the removed particles, providing a water-free cleaning method.

superordinate.label: Enhance contaminant mobilization to reduce rinse water
superordinate.description: Use chemical interactions to detach, solubilize, or disperse soils so contaminants can be removed with minimal water.

superordinate.label: Close-loop water reuse via targeted separation
superordinate.description: Recover and recycle rinse water by separating removed contaminants (and their carrier chemistry) so the same water can be reused safely.

basic.label: Humic-based chelating/dispersing agent for contaminant release
basic.description: Introduce mild, biodegradable humic-like molecules that chelate metal ions and disperse oils/soils, forming soluble or separable complexes that detach from fabric and are easier to rinse.

labels.name: Chelation-assisted solubility
labels.description: Introducing agents that bind metal ions to increase solubility and weaken soil adhesion to fibers.

basic.label: Separation-optimized water purification loop
basic.description: A process loop designed to separate humic–contaminant complexes from rinse water and return purified water to the wash cycle with minimal loss of active chemistry.

labels.name: Immediate fluid reclamation
labels.description: Capturing used vapor or condensate, purifying it locally, and recirculating it directly back into the process.

labels.name: Membrane fluid purification
labels.description: Using semi-permeable membranes to separate water from contaminants and cleaning agents for recovery.

subordinate.label: Engineered or natural humic formulations and dosing
subordinate.description: Concrete implementations: engineered humic acid analogues or naturally derived humic substances, specified biodegradability, mildness, concentration ranges, and dosing strategies to achieve chelation/dispersal without fabric damage.

subordinate.label: Physical/chemical separation technologies and process controls
subordinate.description: Concrete implementations: filtration (micro/ultra), membrane separation, flocculation/settling, adsorption beds, or combined unit operations plus controls tuned to recover humic–dirt complexes and maintain water quality for reuse.

idea: A low-water washing system that uses a mild, biodegradable solution containing engineered humic acid analogues or naturally derived humic substances. These compounds act as powerful chelating and dispersing agents, effectively binding to dirt, oils, and metal ions embedded in fabric. This complexation process makes the contaminants easier to rinse away with a minimal amount of water, which is then purified and recycled through a system optimized to separate the humic-dirt complexes.

superordinate.label: Non‑contact particle detachment via localized pressure dynamics
superordinate.description: Use of rapidly changing, spatially confined air pressure/turbulence to mechanically dislodge dry dirt and lint from fabric fibers without abrasive contact or large-scale airflow.

superordinate.label: Isolation and mechanical decoupling of garments
superordinate.description: Create a controlled, confined environment that holds garments steady and isolates the zone of actuation so micro-scale forces act on fabric rather than moving the whole load or creating bulk airflow.

superordinate.label: Low‑energy capture and containment of released particles
superordinate.description: Continuously remove and contain dislodged particles using minimal background flow and filtration so particles are captured without disturbing ongoing micro‑actuation or using large volumes of air/water.

basic.label: Localized, tunable micro‑pressure actuation
basic.description: An array of small, addressable actuation sources that generate rapid, tunable, non‑linear pressure pulses or vortical micro‑flows targeted at fabric fibers to create micro‑turbulence and pressure differentials that detach particles.

labels.name: Actuated micro-disruption
labels.description: Using small-scale actuators (brushes, piezos) to directly agitate fibers or dislodge particles locally.

basic.label: Suspended garment positioning within a sealed chamber
basic.description: Support and position garments inside an enclosed volume to expose fabric surfaces to localized actuation while minimizing bulk motion and environmental exchange.

labels.name: Aerodynamic suspension
labels.description: Supporting textiles using a regulated air cushion to eliminate contact friction and ensure uniform surface exposure.

labels.name: Controlled environment enclosure
labels.description: A sealed chamber that regulates atmosphere, pressure, and temperature to optimize reaction conditions while containing fluids.

basic.label: Gentle continuous extraction and filtration
basic.description: A low‑velocity background flow that quietly conveys dislodged particles from the local actuation zone into a filtering/collection system without interfering with the localized pressure fields.

labels.name: Laminar shear airflow
labels.description: maintaining non-turbulent, wall-attached airflow to apply persistent, gentle shear forces that detach surface particulates.

subordinate.label: Micro‑jets/pulsators and control parameters
subordinate.description: Concrete implementations: arrays of micro‑nozzles or pulsator elements (mechanical, piezoelectric, MEMS) with controllable frequency/amplitude/phase, programmed actuation patterns to create non‑linear pulses and micro‑turbulence concentrated at fiber scale; includes local sensors and control electronics for tuning.

subordinate.label: Sealed enclosure and hanging apparatus
subordinate.description: Concrete implementations: airtight chamber shell and door, hanger/clamp geometry to suspend garments, acoustic and airflow seals, internal mounts to position micro‑actuators relative to fabric, vibration isolation to prevent bulk movement.

subordinate.label: Low‑flow blower and filter media
subordinate.description: Concrete implementations: low‑noise, low‑velocity fan or microblower providing gentle background flow; HEPA/electrostatic/pleated filters or cyclonic preseparator; tuned flow rates and silencers to quietly capture liberated particles without disrupting localized actuation.

idea: A sealed garment cleaning chamber where clothes are suspended. An array of micro-jets or pulsators generates highly localized, tunable air pressure pulsations around individual fabric fibers. These rapid, non-linear air movements create micro-turbulences and pressure differentials that physically dislodge dry dirt, dust, and lint particles without harsh mechanical contact or significant bulk air movement. Dislodged particles are then quietly drawn into a filter system by a very gentle, continuous background flow.

superordinate.label: Chemically detach soils to enable low-water removal
superordinate.description: Use chemical alteration of soil–fiber interactions so soils lose adhesion and can be removed with minimal water or mechanical action.

superordinate.label: Localized low-volume delivery to minimize water use
superordinate.description: Apply cleaning agents in a targeted, low-volume manner so only contaminated zones receive treatment, reducing total water applied.

superordinate.label: maintain fabric safety and non-toxicity constraints
superordinate.description: Constrain functional choices to materials and processes that preserve fabric integrity, human safety, and environmental acceptability while enabling low-water cleaning.

basic.label: Use of plant-derived solubilizing/emulsifying agents to weaken oil/fat adhesion
basic.description: Introduce amphiphilic or lipophilic-tuned phytochemicals that solubilize or emulsify fatty/waxy soils and reduce their adhesion to fibers, enabling removal with little water.

labels.name: Biocompatible safety formulation
labels.description: Constraining chemical choices to non-toxic, biodegradable ingredients to allow operation without heavy rinsing.

basic.label: Targeted application mechanics (spray/immersion/wipe)
basic.description: Mechanisms and delivery formats that deposit the active agents precisely and with minimal liquid volume (metered sprays, micro-immersion, wipe-on pads, foams).

labels.name: Localized spot-treatment
labels.description: Mechanisms that target specific stained areas, minimizing overall solvent or energy inventory to the required zone.

labels.name: Low-volume localized rinsing
labels.description: Using focused, low-flow fluid application to carry away detached material with minimal water usage.

basic.label: Formulation and material constraints for safety and fabric compatibility
basic.description: Formulation choices and additives (pH buffering, non-reactive concentrations, absence of enzymes/microbes) that ensure non-toxicity, prevent fiber damage or discoloration, and remain biodegradable.

labels.name: Biocompatible safety formulation
labels.description: Constraining chemical choices to non-toxic, biodegradable ingredients to allow operation without heavy rinsing.

subordinate.label: Specific phytochemical implementations and properties
subordinate.description: Examples: saponins (soapnut, quillaja), alkyl glycosides, plant-derived fatty acid esters or glycosides, terpene glycosides; tuned concentrations and HLB for emulsification (e.g., 0.1–5% w/v typical ranges), non-enzymatic mode of action, optimized for fabric fiber affinity and rinseability.

subordinate.label: Concrete delivery formats and parameters
subordinate.description: Metered spray/mist with controlled droplet size (e.g., 50–200 μm), low-volume local immersion trays with short contact + recirculation, pre-wetted wipe cartridges or microfoam dispensers, dosing protocols to limit total water per garment.

subordinate.label: Safety and formulation specifics
subordinate.description: pH buffering, low ionic strength, fabric-safe preservatives/stabilizers, biodegradability requirements, absence of broad-spectrum enzymes/microbes, testing thresholds for colorfastness and tensile strength.

idea: A targeted spray or minimal-water immersion system utilizing specific, non-toxic, fabric-safe plant-derived phytochemicals that are known to solubilize or emulsify fatty/waxy substances, similar to how plant cuticles are degraded. These agents would weaken the adhesion of oily dirt and grime to fabric fibers, allowing for easy removal with minimal water rinsing or wiping, without relying on broad-spectrum enzymes or microbes.

superordinate.label: Concentrated high-energy vapor treatment
superordinate.description: Use of high-temperature vapor in a controlled space to effect cleaning/sterilization by heat and vapor interaction rather than bulk water washing.

superordinate.label: Thermo-vapor contaminant disruption
superordinate.description: Exploit thermal shock and vapor properties to denature biological contaminants, remove odors, and loosen superficial soils/oils.

superordinate.label: On-board closed-loop resource reuse
superordinate.description: Recover and recycle working fluid within the device to minimize net external water input.

superordinate.label: Controlled treatment environment
superordinate.description: Isolate garments and control atmosphere (temperature, humidity, pressure, airflow) to protect items and concentrate process effects.

basic.label: Closed-loop superheated dry-steam generation and circulation
basic.description: Generate vapor above the liquid phase (minimal droplets), rapidly heat a small reservoir, and actively circulate the superheated vapor through garments inside a sealed chamber.

labels.name: Controlled environment enclosure
labels.description: A sealed chamber that regulates atmosphere, pressure, and temperature to optimize reaction conditions while containing fluids.

labels.name: Thermal contaminant desorption
labels.description: Applying controlled heat to drive volatile organics from fibers into the gas phase without solvents.

basic.label: Thermal and vapor-mediated contaminant removal
basic.description: Rely on high temperature exposure and vapor interaction to sterilize, deodorize, and dislodge soils via denaturation and phase-change effects.

labels.name: Thermal contaminant desorption
labels.description: Applying controlled heat to drive volatile organics from fibers into the gas phase without solvents.

basic.label: Condensate capture, filtration, and return
basic.description: Collect condensed vapor, remove particulates/contaminants, and pump the treated liquid back to the reservoir for reuse within the device.

labels.name: Immediate fluid reclamation
labels.description: Capturing used vapor or condensate, purifying it locally, and recirculating it directly back into the process.

basic.label: Sealed cabinet and controlled atmosphere management
basic.description: maintain an enclosed treatment volume with sensors and controls for pressure, temperature, humidity, and airflow to ensure process efficacy and garment safety.

labels.name: Controlled environment enclosure
labels.description: A sealed chamber that regulates atmosphere, pressure, and temperature to optimize reaction conditions while containing fluids.

labels.name: Adaptive process control
labels.description: Systems that detect fabric/soil properties and adjust energy inputs to optimize cleaning while preventing damage.

subordinate.label: Sealed garment cabinet with small heated reservoir and vapor circulation hardware
subordinate.description: Physical cabinet, small contained water reservoir, rapid electric/heater element to create superheated steam, fans/blowers or pumps and ducting to distribute vapor through hanging garments.

subordinate.label: Process parameters and vapor characteristics
subordinate.description: Superheated dry steam (specified temperature and low droplet fraction), dwell time control, temperature spike profiles for thermal shock, and protocols for deodorization/sterilization.

subordinate.label: Condensate handling components
subordinate.description: Condensation surfaces/channels, collection sump, multi-stage filtration (mesh/particulate filter, activated carbon or antimicrobial filter), and recirculation pump or gravity return to reservoir.

subordinate.label: Enclosure seals, sensors, and safety controls
subordinate.description: Gasketed doors, pressure-relief valve, humidity and temperature sensors, control logic, and vents or valves to manage internal atmosphere and protect fabrics.

idea: A sealed garment cabinet that uses a small, contained reservoir of water. This water is rapidly heated to generate superheated, dry steam (vapor without liquid droplets). This superheated steam is circulated through the garments, effectively sterilizing, deodorizing, and loosening superficial dirt and oils through thermal shock and vapor action. The steam then cools, condenses, and is immediately collected, filtered, and returned to the reservoir for continuous reuse, achieving powerful cleaning with extremely low water replenishment.

superordinate.label: Transfer contaminants to a removable carrier
superordinate.description: Achieve textile cleanliness by moving soils and oils off the fabric onto an intentionally removable layer or carrier rather than removing them with bulk solvent.

superordinate.label: Stimulus-controlled release of the carrier
superordinate.description: Use a mild, targeted stimulus to switch the carrier's adhesion state so it detaches and releases entrained contaminants without damaging the textile.

superordinate.label: Dry mechanical recovery of dislodged contaminants
superordinate.description: Recover and separate the detached carrier and entrained soils through mechanical collection and filtration instead of rinsing with water.

basic.label: Temporary contaminant‑binding removable coating
basic.description: A thin, fabric‑compatible coating applied to garments that preferentially adsorbs or encapsulates dirt/oils and is engineered to be removed intact for disposal or filtration.

labels.name: Sacrificial film lift-off
labels.description: Applying a temporary film that entraps surface contaminants as it solidifies and removes them when peeled.

basic.label: Stimulus-responsive delamination mechanism
basic.description: A fabric-safe mechanism by which a controlled stimulus (physical/chemical/optical) causes the coating to delaminate or change phase and release captured soils.

labels.name: Stimulus-responsive capture
labels.description: Using reversible stimuli (charge, light, temp) to adhere debris to a collector and release it into a waste receptacle.

basic.label: Localized vacuum/filtration capture and gentle handling
basic.description: A mechanical system that collects the shed coating and entrained particles, separates them from the garments, and confines waste for disposal or recycling.

labels.name: Ultrasonic cavitation
labels.description: Using ultrasound to drive oscillating micro-bubbles in a thin liquid film, creating localized forces that dislodge contaminants.

labels.name: Negative-pressure vapor extraction
labels.description: maintaining reduced pressure to continuously draw volatile byproducts and contaminants away from the fabric to prevent redeposition.

labels.name: Carrier regeneration
labels.description: Processes designed to separate collected contaminants from the transport medium to prepare the carrier for reuse.

subordinate.label: Dissolvable/detachable nanocoating formulation
subordinate.description: Nanoscale coating chemistry and microstructure engineered with higher affinity for oils/dirt than for fiber surfaces, designed to delaminate or dissolve intact when triggered.

subordinate.label: Specific mild triggers (light, humidity, vibration)
subordinate.description: Concrete trigger implementations such as a defined light wavelength (phototrigger), small controlled humidity changes, or low‑amplitude mechanical vibration to induce coating release.

subordinate.label: Gentle tumbling cabinet plus vacuum and filters
subordinate.description: Processing environment examples: a low-impact tumbling drum or cabinet where delamination occurs paired with integrated vacuum suction and filter cartridges to capture shed coating and soils.

idea: Garments are treated with a dissolvable or detachable nanocoating that has a stronger affinity for dirt/oils than for fabric fibers. After wear, the garments are placed in a gentle tumbling drum or cabinet. A mild, fabric-safe trigger (e.g., a specific light wavelength, a slight humidity change, or a very mild vibration) causes the nanocoating to rapidly delaminate or de-bond from the fabric, encapsulating and releasing the accumulated dirt. The shed nanocoating and dirt particles are then collected by a vacuum and filter system, leaving clean fabric with no water.

superordinate.label: Localized mechanical detachment of contaminants
superordinate.description: Remove soil from fabric by applying targeted, surface-bound mechanical forces at the fabric–surface interface rather than by bulk liquid agitation or solvent action.

superordinate.label: Interface coupling of energy to fabric
superordinate.description: Ensure efficient transfer of mechanical energy into the textile by bringing the fabric into controlled contact or relative motion with an energized surface.

superordinate.label: Dry-phase collection and isolation of removed particles
superordinate.description: Capture and remove dislodged particles from the cleaning zone using an air-based collection/separation pathway rather than relying on aqueous transport.

basic.label: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) transduction at the fabric interface
basic.description: Generate high-frequency, surface-propagating mechanical waves on a contact surface to exert localized, oscillatory forces on contaminant particles at the fabric surface, causing detachment without bulk liquid.

labels.name: Acoustic radiation force
labels.description: Using acoustic pressure fields to move or aggregate suspended particles independently of bulk flow.

basic.label: Mechanical/contact coupling mechanism
basic.description: Provide and control the physical contact conditions (pressure, conformity, relative motion) between fabric and the energized surface so that SAWs or other surface vibrations effectively transfer energy into the textile.

labels.name: Kinematic energy coupling
labels.description: Designing the mechanical interface to transmit tumbling motion into fabric strain or actuator energy efficiently.

basic.label: Air-suction collection and separation
basic.description: Remove and contain particles once detached by aspirating them away from the interface and separating solids from the airflow for disposal or filtering.

labels.name: Negative-pressure vapor extraction
labels.description: maintaining reduced pressure to continuously draw volatile byproducts and contaminants away from the fabric to prevent redeposition.

subordinate.label: Piezoelectric SAW surface: interdigitated electrodes on piezoelectric lining
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation: a drum or plate lined with piezoelectric material (e.g., PZT, PVDF) patterned with interdigitated electrodes to launch high-frequency surface acoustic waves (specified kHz–MHz range, electrode pitch and aperture tuned for wavelength), driven by power electronics and control circuitry.

subordinate.label: Drum/plate geometry and contact mechanisms
subordinate.description: Examples: textured or compliant drum lining that presses/gently tumbled fabric against the SAW surface; tensioning or holding mechanisms, rollers or agitators, controlled pressure settings and relative motion profiles to optimize coupling without damaging textiles.

subordinate.label: Integrated vacuum and filtration module
subordinate.description: Examples: suction ports positioned at the interface edge, vacuum pump and air ducting, particle separator or filter cartridge (e.g., cyclonic separator, HEPA or washable filter), collection bin for captured dirt, and controls to synchronize suction with SAW activation.

idea: A specialized cleaning plate or drum lining made of a piezoelectric material. Clothes are gently pressed against or tumbled on this surface. Interdigitated electrodes on the surface generate high-frequency SAWs that propagate along the interface with the fabric. These SAWs exert precise, localized mechanical forces on dirt particles at the fabric surface, effectively "sweeping" or "vibrating" them off without needing bulk water, solvents, or bulk ultrasonic cavitation. The dislodged dirt is collected by an integrated vacuum system.

superordinate.label: Non‑fluid force–based particulate removal
superordinate.description: Remove or relocate particulate soil from textiles using forces other than liquid solvent action (e.g., electrostatic forces) to separate contaminants from fabric surfaces or move them to a collection site.

basic.label: Embedded electrostatic field generation to mobilize particles
basic.description: Integrate materials that produce persistent or mechanically recharged electric fields in or on fabric so that generated Coulombic/field forces cause charged or polar particles to be repelled from, or attracted along controlled paths away from, the textile surface and toward a capture region.

labels.name: Electrokinetic soil migration
labels.description: Applying an electric field to drive charged soil particles (electrophoresis) out of the textile structure.

labels.name: Electrostatic charge optimization
labels.description: Controlling humidity/surface conditions to maximize charge generation for particle attraction while managing dissipation.

subordinate.label: Electret materials, fabric liners and removable collectors
subordinate.description: Concrete implementations such as electret polymers embedded in fibers, electret-coated liners or bonded electret films in garments, design parameters like charge density and retention, activation by tumbling/agitation, and a dedicated removable/replaceable collection component (pocket, filter, or adhesive pad) that accumulates attracted particles.

idea: Design fabrics or fabric liners with embedded electret properties. As clothes tumble or are gently agitated in a dry environment, the electret material actively generates electric fields that either repel charged dust and dirt particles from the fabric surface or attract them to a dedicated, removable collection component, effectively cleaning without water.

superordinate.label: Dry mechanical extraction of embedded particulates
superordinate.description: Remove dirt, dust, and particulates from textiles by direct mechanical interaction rather than dissolving or flushing with liquids or chemicals.

superordinate.label: Enable repeated controlled contact between fabric and active surfaces
superordinate.description: Create relative motion and contact forces that bring fabric into and across extraction surfaces frequently and gently to dislodge particles.

superordinate.label: Capture and contain dislodged particles without solvents
superordinate.description: Collect, retain, and remove particulate matter after mechanical extraction in a dry state so it does not re-deposit on garments.

superordinate.label: Protect fabric integrity while penetrating weave
superordinate.description: Balance penetration and contact effectiveness with material compliance and limits so fibers are not damaged while particles are lifted.

basic.label: Micro-projection contact extraction
basic.description: Use arrays of small, fabric-safe projections (micro-needles / textured bumps) on internal surfaces to physically engage, penetrate interstices, and lift embedded particulates from fabric fibers.

labels.name: Dry mechanical grooming
labels.description: Using engineered protrusions to physically lift or scrape dry debris and lint without fluid.

labels.name: Actuated micro-disruption
labels.description: Using small-scale actuators (brushes, piezos) to directly agitate fibers or dislodge particles locally.

basic.label: Motion and contact mechanics
basic.description: Apply controlled kinematics (tumbling, rotation, brushing, oscillation) and contact pressure to ensure fabric repeatedly contacts the active extraction surfaces.

labels.name: Kinematic energy coupling
labels.description: Designing the mechanical interface to transmit tumbling motion into fabric strain or actuator energy efficiently.

basic.label: Dry particle capture and containment
basic.description: Provide mechanisms to trap, filter, or remove particles after they are dislodged so they do not remain in the appliance or reattach to clothing.

basic.label: Compliance and penetration control
basic.description: Control projection compliance, tip shape, spacing, and contact depth/pressure to maximize particle extraction while minimizing fiber damage.

labels.name: Adaptive process control
labels.description: Systems that detect fabric/soil properties and adjust energy inputs to optimize cleaning while preventing damage.

subordinate.label: Soft micro-needles / textured micro-projections
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation: arrays of soft polymeric, silicone, or microfiber-tipped micro-needles or textured projections mounted on rotating pads or drum interiors; characterized by tip radius, length, density, and material compliance to penetrate weave and lift particulates.

subordinate.label: Rotating pads / tumbling / brushing mechanisms
subordinate.description: Concrete implementations: rotating or oscillating textured pads, a tumbling drum with patterned interior surfaces, controlled speed/pressure profiles, and cycles tuned for gentle repeated rubbing.

subordinate.label: Removable lint traps, filters, and suction-assisted bins
subordinate.description: Concrete implementations: detachable debris collection trays, multi-stage filters, HEPA or mesh filters, optional low-power vacuum channels or one-way airflow to transport and isolate dislodged particulates.

subordinate.label: Rounded tips, compliant materials, and pressure control
subordinate.description: Concrete implementations: projection tip geometries with limited sharpness, elastic backing layers, adjustable contact pressure settings, and spacing/length specifications to limit fiber abrasion while allowing penetration into weave.

idea: A laundry appliance with internal surfaces or rotating pads featuring arrays of soft, fabric-safe micro-needles or textured micro-projections. As garments are gently tumbled or brushed against these surfaces, the micro-needles penetrate the weave, physically lifting and extracting deeply embedded dirt, dust, and particulate matter from the fabric pores without requiring water or harsh chemicals.

superordinate.label: Selective capture-and-remove instead of bulk solvent washing
superordinate.description: Replace broad, water-intensive dissolution of soils with targeted capture of contaminants onto applied agents that are later removed, minimizing use of bulk solvent.

superordinate.label: Localized deposition of treatment
superordinate.description: Deliver cleaning agents directly and sparsely to the textile surface in a controlled, localized form rather than immersing the whole garment.

superordinate.label: Triggered detachment and collection
superordinate.description: Use a controlled external trigger to cause the capture agents to release or disintegrate in a way that carries away bound contaminants into a collection stream, enabling removal without rinsing.

superordinate.label: Process-state conditioning to enable reversible binding
superordinate.description: Manage environmental and timing conditions (e.g., humidity, dwell time) to favor contaminant capture first and then subsequent release when triggered.

basic.label: Engineered biodegradable particulate binding agents
basic.description: Microscopic particulate scaffolds engineered with high chemical/physical affinity for target soils and odor molecules that capture contaminants from textile fibers and carry them when removed.

labels.name: Active-release micro-reservoirs
labels.description: Integrating discrete payload carriers into the textile that release cleaning agents upon triggering.

labels.name: Micro-abrasive extraction
labels.description: Using fine, benign solid particles to physically abrade or carry soil away via direct contact mechanics.

basic.label: Aerosol/mist-based application system
basic.description: A mechanism for producing and depositing a fine mist of the particulate agents onto garments to achieve uniform, low-volume coverage.

labels.name: Atomized mist application
labels.description: Delivering cleaning agents via fine mist to solubilize soils with minimal fluid volume.

basic.label: Controlled trigger for particle detachment/degradation and collection subsystem
basic.description: A low-energy, specific trigger (e.g., wavelength-specific light, gentle vibration) that initiates predictable particle detachment or degradation combined with a collection path to remove particulates and bound contaminants.

labels.name: Stimulus-responsive capture
labels.description: Using reversible stimuli (charge, light, temp) to adhere debris to a collector and release it into a waste receptacle.

basic.label: Environmental dwell and conditioning control
basic.description: Temporal and atmospheric control (e.g., reduced humidity, set dwell time) applied after deposition to promote stable binding of contaminants prior to triggering release.

labels.name: Controlled environment enclosure
labels.description: A sealed chamber that regulates atmosphere, pressure, and temperature to optimize reaction conditions while containing fluids.

subordinate.label: Decellularized biodegradable bio-scaffold particles with tailored binding sites
subordinate.description: Specific implementation: microscopic decellularized bio-scaffold particles (biodegradable, nonliving) engineered or functionalized to present chemical groups that selectively adsorb organic soils and volatile odor molecules.

subordinate.label: Fine mist atomizer parameters and delivery pattern
subordinate.description: Specific implementation: an atomizer/nozzle producing droplets or dry-carrier aerosol in the sub-10–100 µm range with controlled dosage, spray pattern, and traversal to cover garments without pooling water.

subordinate.label: Low-energy optical or mechanical trigger and particulate collection design
subordinate.description: Specific implementation: calibrated LED or laser wavelengths or low-amplitude vibrational actuators that induce scaffold degradation/detachment, paired with a vacuum/filtration collection chamber that captures released particles and encapsulated contaminants.

subordinate.label: Low-humidity dwell conditions and timing
subordinate.description: Specific implementation: controlled chamber environment maintaining reduced relative humidity for a defined dwell period (minutes) to allow particle adhesion and stabilization before activation of the trigger.

idea: A system that applies a fine mist containing microscopic, biodegradable, decellularized bio-scaffold particles onto clothes. These particles are engineered to have a high affinity for common organic dirt and odors. After a short dwell time in a low-humidity environment, a mild trigger (e.g., specific light, very gentle vibration) initiates the controlled degradation or detachment of the bio-scaffold, taking the encapsulated dirt and odor molecules with it into a collection system, leaving clean garments with minimal water usage.

superordinate.label: On-device water recovery and recirculation
superordinate.description: Minimize fresh-water consumption by treating and reusing wash water within the washing system rather than discarding it.

superordinate.label: Passive separation driven by osmotic gradients
superordinate.description: Use solute concentration differences to drive selective transport of water across a barrier without applying hydraulic pressure.

superordinate.label: Concentrate and isolate contaminants for disposal or regeneration
superordinate.description: Separate and retain dirt, detergents, and suspended solids into a smaller-volume stream so they can be removed or treated separately.

superordinate.label: Minimized-input cleaning stage
superordinate.description: Reduce the initial water demand for soil removal to lower the volume of water that must be purified and recycled.

basic.label: Closed-loop water recycling subsystem
basic.description: Circulate purified water back into the wash cycle using storage, pumps, and valves to maintain continuous reuse.

labels.name: Immediate fluid reclamation
labels.description: Capturing used vapor or condensate, purifying it locally, and recirculating it directly back into the process.

labels.name: Membrane fluid purification
labels.description: Using semi-permeable membranes to separate water from contaminants and cleaning agents for recovery.

basic.label: Forward osmosis membrane separation (osmotic purification)
basic.description: Employ a semi-permeable membrane and a concentrated draw solution so water migrates from greywater into the draw side, leaving contaminants behind.

labels.name: Osmotic extraction gradient
labels.description: Creating a chemical-potential differential between fabric and a concentrated medium to draw water and solutes out of fibers.

labels.name: Membrane fluid purification
labels.description: Using semi-permeable membranes to separate water from contaminants and cleaning agents for recovery.

basic.label: Feed-side contaminant concentration and handling
basic.description: Accumulate solids, soils, and concentrated detergent residues on the feed side and manage that concentrated waste for disposal or further treatment.

labels.name: Carrier regeneration
labels.description: Processes designed to separate collected contaminants from the transport medium to prepare the carrier for reuse.

basic.label: Low-water mechanical wash pre-cycle
basic.description: Perform an initial wash that uses greatly reduced water volume (e.g., short duration, high agitation) to remove bulk soils before purification.

labels.name: Low-volume localized rinsing
labels.description: Using focused, low-flow fluid application to carry away detached material with minimal water usage.

subordinate.label: Pumps, storage tanks, valves, and control logic
subordinate.description: Concrete components and control sequences that capture FO permeate, store treated water, and reintroduce it into wash cycles (e.g., recirculation pump, buffer tank, solenoid valves, PLC).

subordinate.label: FO membrane assembly and reusable draw solution
subordinate.description: Specific technologies: thin‑film composite forward osmosis membrane module paired with a highly concentrated reusable draw solution (e.g., brine or engineered draw solutes) and associated feed/draw plumbing.

subordinate.label: Concentrate collection and disposal/regeneration unit
subordinate.description: Physical instantiation for the concentrated feed (e.g., small holding tank, periodic purge valve, optional downstream treatment like biofilter or sludge removal).

subordinate.label: Reduced-volume cycle parameters and mechanical agitation hardware
subordinate.description: Concrete settings and components enabling a low-water prewash (e.g., specific drum motion profiles, short cycle time, water volume per load estimate).

idea: A washing machine integrated with a forward osmosis system. After an initial, minimal-water wash cycle, the greywater (feed solution) is pumped to one side of an FO membrane. A highly concentrated, reusable draw solution is on the other side. Clean water is naturally pulled from the greywater through the membrane, leaving all contaminants and dirt in the concentrated feed solution, and the purified water is then recycled back into the wash system for continuous reuse, drastically reducing fresh water consumption.

superordinate.label: Non-contact, fluid-mediated particulate removal
superordinate.description: Use of controlled airflows to dislodge and transport surface particles without liquids or mechanical abrasion.

superordinate.label: Contact elimination via suspension
superordinate.description: Support the garment on an air cushion to remove normal contact/friction and expose surfaces for cleaning.

superordinate.label: Containment and separation of extracted contaminants
superordinate.description: Capture and isolate removed particles from the working airflow to prevent re-deposition and enable disposal or filtration.

superordinate.label: Localized, adaptive flow targeting
superordinate.description: Precisely direct and modulate airflow spatially and temporally to address varied fabric geometry and soil distribution.

basic.label: Directed high-velocity airflow and localized suction for particle extraction
basic.description: Targeted jets and localized vacuum/siphon actions lift lint, dust and superficial grime from fibers and entrain them into a removal stream.

labels.name: Laminar shear airflow
labels.description: maintaining non-turbulent, wall-attached airflow to apply persistent, gentle shear forces that detach surface particulates.

labels.name: Negative-pressure vapor extraction
labels.description: maintaining reduced pressure to continuously draw volatile byproducts and contaminants away from the fabric to prevent redeposition.

basic.label: Controlled air-cushion support (air film)
basic.description: A precisely regulated upward airflow layer that suspends textiles to eliminate contact forces and enable unobstructed exposure of surfaces.

labels.name: Aerodynamic suspension
labels.description: Supporting textiles using a regulated air cushion to eliminate contact friction and ensure uniform surface exposure.

basic.label: Filtration and particle collection subsystem
basic.description: Mechanisms to separate, trap and store airborne particulates removed by the airflow (filters, cyclones, bins), preventing recirculation.

basic.label: Flow control, sensing, and targeting mechanisms
basic.description: Sensors, valves, nozzle positioning and control logic that spatially and temporally shape airflow to optimize extraction while protecting fabrics.

labels.name: Adaptive process control
labels.description: Systems that detect fabric/soil properties and adjust energy inputs to optimize cleaning while preventing damage.

subordinate.label: Nozzles and localized suction hardware
subordinate.description: Implementations such as high-velocity air jets, pulsed or steady streams, siphon-like vacuum ports, nozzle geometries, mounting arrays and operating pressures/flow rates configured to lift and entrain particles from fabric surfaces.

subordinate.label: Air-cushion generation components
subordinate.description: Perforated plenums or porous membranes, adjustable blowers/pressure regulators, skirts or containment flanges, pressure sensors and flow-rate settings that create a stable air film beneath garments.

subordinate.label: Filters, separators and containment
subordinate.description: HEPA/pleated or washable pre-filters, cyclonic separators, filter housings, removable collection bins, possible electrostatic precipitators and routing for disposal or exhaust/recirculation.

subordinate.label: Sensors, actuators and control logic
subordinate.description: Optical/particulate sensors, pressure and flow sensors, microcontroller/PLC, servo or solenoid valve actuators, nozzle positioners, algorithms for pulsing/scan patterns and user-control interfaces.

idea: A cleaning chamber where garments are introduced and suspended on a precisely controlled air cushion (an "air film") generated from below. This eliminates friction and mechanical wear. While suspended, targeted, high-velocity air nozzles (acting as siphons or localized vacuums) are directed at the garment from above, actively lifting and extracting dry dust, lint, and superficial grime from the fabric fibers, collecting them in a filter system, all without water or direct contact.

superordinate.label: Localized encapsulation-and-extraction
