subordinate.label: Multispectral imaging and stain-detection algorithms
subordinate.description: Concrete sensors and software: multispectral/ hyperspectral or camera+LED setups, reflectance/spectral analysis, and image-processing to generate an actionable target map.

subordinate.label: Low-power pulsed laser with tunable wavelength and pulse energy; beam-scanning delivery
subordinate.description: Specific hardware and parameters: solid-state or fiber lasers, selectable wavelengths matched to stain chromophores, controlled pulse duration/energy to cause micro‑vaporization or photothermal/photochemical decomposition without fiber damage.

subordinate.label: Gentle nozzle vacuum with filters and containment
subordinate.description: Practical extraction: low-flow vacuum nozzle co-located with treatment spot, filtration or adsorption stages to capture particulates and condensates, integrated waste containment.

idea: A garment cleaning station equipped with a low-power, pulsed laser system. Optical sensors identify soiled areas, and the laser is precisely tuned (wavelength, pulse energy) to be selectively absorbed by common dirt, oils, or stain chromophores. The absorbed energy causes rapid, localized micro-vaporization or thermal decomposition of the contaminant, effectively "ablating" it from the fabric surface without heating or damaging the surrounding fibers. A gentle vacuum collects the resulting microscopic debris, providing an extremely targeted, water-free, and residue-free cleaning method.

superordinate.label: Reduce water by chemically freeing bound contaminants
superordinate.description: Use biochemical action to break the bonds that hold microbes, biofilms, and trapped odor/dirt compounds to fabrics so they can be removed without soaking or bulk rinsing.

superordinate.label: Localize treatment to minimize resource use
superordinate.description: Deliver treatment only where needed on garments to avoid applying large volumes of liquid to the whole item.

superordinate.label: Non-bulk mechanical capture of loosened material
superordinate.description: Use low-water mechanical or airflow-based methods to pick up or capture residues after they have been loosened from fabric.

basic.label: Targeted biochemical disruption of biofilms/odor matrices
basic.description: Apply biological or chemical agents that specifically degrade the extracellular matrix and bound compounds of microbial biofilms and stubborn soils, rendering them detach-able from fibers.

labels.name: Biological soil metabolism
labels.description: Applying biological agents or enzymes to metabolically consume or break down organic soils over time.

basic.label: Precision spray/mist delivery
basic.description: A delivery mechanism that creates a controlled fine mist or directed spray to apply small volumes of treatment accurately to contaminated areas.

labels.name: Atomized mist application
labels.description: Delivering cleaning agents via fine mist to solubilize soils with minimal fluid volume.

labels.name: Localized spot-treatment
labels.description: Mechanisms that target specific stained areas, minimizing overall solvent or energy inventory to the required zone.

basic.label: Low-moisture removal and capture
basic.description: Methods for removing or collecting loosened contaminants without full washing, such as localized wiping or airflow with filtration.

labels.name: Thin-film peel removal
labels.description: Applying a minimal liquid layer to entrap soil, followed by mechanical removal (wiping/peeling) rather than dilution.

labels.name: Negative-pressure vapor extraction
labels.description: maintaining reduced pressure to continuously draw volatile byproducts and contaminants away from the fabric to prevent redeposition.

subordinate.label: Enzymes, dispersants, and bacteriophages
subordinate.description: Specific agents: biofilm‑dispersing enzymes (e.g., DNase, proteases, polysaccharidases), mild natural dispersants/surfactants, or lytic bacteriophages formulated for fabric-safe topical application.

subordinate.label: Fine‑mist hardware and dosing control
subordinate.description: Nozzle designs and actuators that produce controlled droplet size and volume (e.g., atomizing spray heads, aerosol cartridges, programmable pulse dosing) and targeted aiming or masks.

subordinate.label: Wiping and airflow filtration components
subordinate.description: Concrete removal implementations like damp microfiber pads, guided wiping tools, gentle air jets or suction combined with particle/odour capture filters (HEPA, activated carbon) or electrostatic collectors.

idea: A targeted spray or fine mist system that applies a fabric-safe mixture of biofilm-dispersing enzymes, mild natural dispersants, or lytic bacteriophages onto garments. This treatment specifically breaks down the sticky matrix of microbial biofilms and the embedded dirt/odor compounds, allowing them to be easily wiped away with a damp cloth or lifted by a gentle air current and filtration system, significantly reducing the need for bulk water washing to eliminate persistent smells and grime.

superordinate.label: Localized energy-induced detachment
superordinate.description: Use focused energy to create localized mechanical perturbations that break adhesive bonds between contaminants and fabric.

superordinate.label: Dry removal and containment
superordinate.description: Collect and isolate dislodged particles via airflow and filtration so contaminants are removed without liquid washing.

superordinate.label: Controlled, damage-minimizing delivery
superordinate.description: Precisely control and time the energy delivery with sensing and safeguards to maximize detachment while preventing material damage.

basic.label: Targeted micro-scale mechanical disruption via pulsed electrical energy
basic.description: Convert pulsed electrical energy at or near the fabric surface into localized micro-mechanical shockwaves or impulses at the fabric–contaminant interface to sever adhesive bonds.

labels.name: Thermoelastic shock disruption
labels.description: Inducing rapid thermal expansion/contraction to generate micro-scale shockwaves that break adhesive bonds between soil and fiber.

labels.name: Actuated micro-disruption
labels.description: Using small-scale actuators (brushes, piezos) to directly agitate fibers or dislodge particles locally.

basic.label: Vacuum-driven particle extraction and filtration
basic.description: Use gentle directed airflow to lift, transport, and capture dislodged particles into a filtration/collection subsystem for removal and containment.

labels.name: Membrane fluid purification
labels.description: Using semi-permeable membranes to separate water from contaminants and cleaning agents for recovery.

labels.name: Negative-pressure vapor extraction
labels.description: maintaining reduced pressure to continuously draw volatile byproducts and contaminants away from the fabric to prevent redeposition.

basic.label: Feedback-controlled sensing and pulse modulation
basic.description: Detect presence, proximity, and response of fabric/contaminants and adapt pulse parameters in closed-loop to ensure effectiveness and avoid fiber damage.

labels.name: Adaptive process control
labels.description: Systems that detect fabric/soil properties and adjust energy inputs to optimize cleaning while preventing damage.

subordinate.label: Embedded micro-electrodes and pulsed-energy parameters
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation: electrodes placed adjacent to fabric within a drum/cabinet; short, high-energy electrical pulses (specified voltage, current, pulse width, repetition rate) tuned to create microshockwaves at the fabric–dirt interface while limiting thermal and electrical stress to fibers.

subordinate.label: Low-flow vacuum, ducts, and filtration modules
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation: low-pressure vacuum pump, airflow channels integrated into drum, pre-filter and fine filter or cyclonic/HEPA collection canister, and removable waste cartridge for trapped particles.

subordinate.label: Sensors, control electronics, and safety interlocks
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation: proximity/pressure/current sensors, current/voltage monitors, microcontroller or DSP for closed-loop pulse shaping, firmware profiles, insulation/grounding and hardware interlocks to prevent unsafe pulses.

idea: A specialized laundry drum or cabinet with embedded micro-electrodes near the fabric surface. When clothes are present, a precisely controlled, short, high-energy electrical pulse is applied. This generates localized, micro-scale mechanical shockwaves within the fabric itself or at the fabric-dirt interface, effectively breaking the adhesive bonds of embedded dirt and grime without damaging the fibers. The dislodged particles are then removed by a gentle vacuum and filtration system, providing a water-free cleaning method that targets deeply embedded contaminants.

superordinate.label: Use interfacial selectivity to transfer contaminants to a removable phase
superordinate.description: Exploit differences in surface chemistry (e.g., hydrophobicity) so soils preferentially attach to a separate phase that can be physically separated from textiles.

superordinate.label: Concentrate contaminants into a separable phase for extraction
superordinate.description: Aggregate and collect soils into a distinct, extractable medium rather than diluting them through large solvent volumes.

superordinate.label: Minimize solvent volume and enable reuse
superordinate.description: Reduce the volume of cleaning fluid in contact with textiles and maintain cleaning performance by recirculating and treating the fluid.

superordinate.label: Protect fabrics by reducing mechanical stress
superordinate.description: Favor chemical or interfacial mechanisms over strong mechanical agitation to detach soils, preserving garment integrity.

basic.label: Microbubble-mediated selective adhesion and flotation separation
basic.description: Generate and introduce microscopic gas bubbles that preferentially adhere to hydrophobic oils/grease on fabric; buoyant bubble–soil complexes rise and separate from garments.

labels.name: Microbubble flotation
labels.description: Introducing gas bubbles that selectively attach to hydrophobic soils, lifting them to the surface for removal.

basic.label: Continuous froth accumulation and removal
basic.description: maintain a contaminant-rich froth layer at the liquid surface and remove it continuously to extract concentrated soils and avoid recontamination.

labels.name: Dense foam transport
labels.description: Utilizing stable, concentrated foam to emulsify soils and carry them away with minimal water.

basic.label: Low-volume immersion with recirculation and treatment
basic.description: Operate in a minimal-volume cleaning chamber and recirculate the liquid through filtration or treatment so the same water is reused while maintaining cleanliness.

labels.name: Immediate fluid reclamation
labels.description: Capturing used vapor or condensate, purifying it locally, and recirculating it directly back into the process.

labels.name: Fluid-minimizing containment
labels.description: Designing geometries that restrict fluid contact to specific pockets or channels, preventing full immersion.

basic.label: Reliance on interfacial mechanisms over bulk mechanical agitation
basic.description: Use adhesion and buoyancy-driven separation to remove soils, minimizing tumbling, shear, or agitation of fabrics.

labels.name: Microbubble flotation
labels.description: Introducing gas bubbles that selectively attach to hydrophobic soils, lifting them to the surface for removal.

labels.name: Electro-coagulation separation
labels.description: Using electrochemical processes to aggregate suspended contaminants into flocs for mechanical separation.

subordinate.label: Bubble generation and surface tuning; froth behavior
subordinate.description: Implementations: ultrafine air/gas bubble generation via spargers, venturi, cavitation or electrolysis; adjust bubble surface properties with surfactants/coatings to enhance hydrophobic soil pickup; control bubble size distribution and stability to form a skimmable froth.

subordinate.label: Skimming and filtration hardware and control
subordinate.description: Concrete mechanisms: surface skimmers, overflow weirs, suction removal, conveyors or continuous froth conveyors; filters and coalescers to concentrate and trap removed soils; waste handling and dewatering of collected froth.

subordinate.label: Compact chamber, pumps, sensors, and treatment modules
subordinate.description: Small-volume washing chamber sized to load, recirculation pumps, particle/chemical filters, possible dosing (surfactant, enzymes) or treatment (UV, adsorption) and sensors to monitor water quality and control reuse.

subordinate.label: Gentle handling systems and agitation limits
subordinate.description: Concrete choices: limited or no tumbling, soft fixtures to separate garments, low-speed gentle flow patterns, and control algorithms that keep mechanical forces minimal.

idea: A low-water garment cleaning chamber where clothes are immersed in a minimal volume of specialized, mildly aqueous solution. Fine, microscopic air bubbles are then introduced into the solution. These bubbles are engineered to selectively adhere to hydrophobic dirt, oils, and grease particles embedded in the fabric. The dirt-laden bubbles rise to the surface, forming a stable "froth" that is continuously skimmed off and filtered, effectively extracting contaminants from the garments with extremely low water usage and minimal mechanical agitation. The cleaned water is then recirculated.

superordinate.label: Non-aqueous contaminant removal by phase-change
superordinate.description: Remove odor-causing and light organic residues from textiles by converting them from bound/embedded states into mobile vapor phase so they can be separated from the garment without water.

superordinate.label: Gentle preservation of textile integrity
superordinate.description: Refresh garments while minimizing mechanical, chemical, and thermal stress to extend wear life and reduce full wet-washes.

superordinate.label: Contained capture and safe neutralization of liberated contaminants
superordinate.description: Prevent re-deposition or environmental release of volatilized contaminants by directing them to capture and/or chemical breakdown systems inside a closed processing environment.

basic.label: Controlled thermal desorption of contaminants
basic.description: Apply precisely controlled, low-level heat to garments to desorb volatile and semi-volatile organics and oils from fibers into the gas phase without using solvents or immersion.

labels.name: Thermal contaminant desorption
labels.description: Applying controlled heat to drive volatile organics from fibers into the gas phase without solvents.

basic.label: Non-reactive, low-stress processing environment
basic.description: maintain a dry, inert or low-oxygen atmosphere, controlled humidity, and gentle mechanical support/handling to avoid oxidation and physical damage while desorption occurs.

labels.name: Controlled environment enclosure
labels.description: A sealed chamber that regulates atmosphere, pressure, and temperature to optimize reaction conditions while containing fluids.

labels.name: Hypoxic biological inhibition
labels.description: maintaining a low-oxygen atmosphere to metabolically stifle the growth of odor-causing microbes.

basic.label: Airflow-mediated transport and capture/neutralization
basic.description: Use continuous, gentle airflow to carry desorbed species away from textiles to filtration and/or catalytic systems that trap or chemically break down contaminants.

labels.name: Laminar shear airflow
labels.description: maintaining non-turbulent, wall-attached airflow to apply persistent, gentle shear forces that detach surface particulates.

labels.name: Carrier regeneration
labels.description: Processes designed to separate collected contaminants from the transport medium to prepare the carrier for reuse.

subordinate.label: Sealed cabinet with low-temperature heaters and precise controls
subordinate.description: A sealed garment chamber with low-temperature heating elements, temperature sensors and controllers, timed cycles, and insulation to achieve uniform, gentle heating sufficient for desorption (implementation of B1).

subordinate.label: Dry/inert gas environment and gentle garment support
subordinate.description: Implementation options such as nitrogen or dehumidified air purge, humidity control, hangers or cradles to minimize mechanical stress, and materials/finish choices that resist heat and inert gases (implementation of B2).

subordinate.label: Fans, filters, and catalytic oxidation unit
subordinate.description: Concrete components like low-speed fans for gentle airflow, particulate and adsorbent filters (e.g., HEPA/activated carbon), and/or a small catalytic oxidizer or thermal-catalytic unit to decompose organics, with exhaust handling (implementation of B3).

idea: A sealed garment cabinet designed to gently heat clothes to a precisely controlled, low temperature in a dry, inert atmosphere. This controlled heating causes volatile odor-causing compounds, body oils, and light organic residues embedded in the fabric to desorb (vaporize) from the fibers. A continuous, gentle airflow then carries these volatilized contaminants to a filtration or catalytic oxidation unit for capture and safe breakdown, effectively refreshing and deodorizing garments without the use of water or chemicals, extending wear time between wet washes.

superordinate.label: Replace bulk immersion with spot-specific chemistry
superordinate.description: Achieve cleaning by applying chemical action only where contamination exists, avoiding treating the whole garment.

superordinate.label: Selective contamination detection
superordinate.description: Identify and localize stains or soiled regions so interventions are directed precisely to affected areas.

superordinate.label: Localized removal of treatment and contaminants without full rinsing
superordinate.description: Extract or evaporate applied solution and mobilized soils locally so no bulk water rinse is required.

superordinate.label: Closed-loop, resource-minimizing treatment cycle
superordinate.description: Coordinate sensing, dosing, dwell, and removal in an automated sequence to minimize resource use and adapt to fabric/stain conditions.

basic.label: Targeted micro-dispensing of concentrated cleaning agent
basic.description: Precisely deposit metered, high-concentration cleaning micro-droplets only onto detected stains to provide required chemistry with minimal liquid volume.

labels.name: Localized spot-treatment
labels.description: Mechanisms that target specific stained areas, minimizing overall solvent or energy inventory to the required zone.

labels.name: Atomized mist application
labels.description: Delivering cleaning agents via fine mist to solubilize soils with minimal fluid volume.

basic.label: Optical sensing and image-based localization
basic.description: Use optical measurements and vision algorithms to detect presence, size, and position of stains and to create a treatment map.

labels.name: Optical residue detection
labels.description: Using sensors to identify specific locations of remaining organic residue for targeted cleaning.

labels.name: Robotic positioning
labels.description: Integrating automated actuators to navigate cleaning tools to specific coordinates for autonomous spot treatment.

basic.label: Localized thermal and suction extraction
basic.description: Remove applied fluid and mobilized soil by combining focused heating/evaporation and targeted vacuum/extraction at the spot.

labels.name: Thermal-suction extraction
labels.description: Combining localized heating (evaporation) with vacuum extraction to mobilize and remove fluid and soil simultaneously.

labels.name: Localized spot-treatment
labels.description: Mechanisms that target specific stained areas, minimizing overall solvent or energy inventory to the required zone.

basic.label: Control and integration for spot treatment cycles
basic.description: Control logic, timing, feedback, and user/device interfaces that sequence sensing, dispensing, dwell, and removal and define device form factor.

labels.name: Adaptive process control
labels.description: Systems that detect fabric/soil properties and adjust energy inputs to optimize cleaning while preventing damage.

subordinate.label: Inkjet-style micro-nozzles and concentrated fabric-safe chemistries
subordinate.description: Piezo or thermal inkjet micro-nozzles, droplet volumes (picoliter–nanoliter), metering valves, concentrated enzyme/solvent formulations and fabric-safe surfactants; dosing parameters tuned by fabric/stain type.

subordinate.label: Multispectral/fluorescence cameras and CV models
subordinate.description: CMOS/CCD camera with LED illumination (visible/UV/IR), fluorescence or reflectance sensors, machine-learning stain classifiers, and algorithms producing a spatial treatment map (coordinates, size, severity).

subordinate.label: Focused warm-air nozzles and micro-vacuum channels
subordinate.description: Localized warm-air jets (temperature and flow controls), micro-vacuum motor and sealed extraction nozzle, particulate/waste capture filters, and airflow/power specifications for rapid evaporation and suction.

subordinate.label: Embedded controller, feedback sensors, and handheld/appliance form factors
subordinate.description: Microcontroller/firmware, user UI (buttons/display/mobile app), moisture/visual feedback sensors to confirm removal, power source (battery or mains), ergonomic handheld or integrated appliance housings, and safety interlocks.

idea: A smart appliance or handheld device that uses optical sensors to detect stains. It then precisely "inkjets" micro-droplets of a concentrated, fabric-safe cleaning solution onto the stain. After a brief dwell time, a focused burst of warm air or a micro-vacuum system rapidly evaporates the liquid and lifts the dissolved/suspended dirt, requiring minimal cleaning fluid and no bulk water rinsing.

superordinate.label: Targeted physical disruption of contaminant structures
superordinate.description: Use localized energy to transiently break down biological matrices and physical bonds that hold soils to fabric, making soils removable without bulk fluid action.

superordinate.label: Chemical/aqueous pre-conditioning to loosen soils
superordinate.description: Apply a brief, fabric-safe wetting or conditioning step that solubilizes, swells, or plasticizes soils and biofilms to reduce adhesion prior to active disruption.

superordinate.label: Minimized fluid removal via targeted rinsing
superordinate.description: Combine pre-conditioning and disruption with a low-volume, targeted rinse strategy so detached soils are removed with substantially less water and mechanical agitation.

basic.label: Pulsed electric-field disruption of biofilms and adhesive bonds
basic.description: Apply pulsed electric fields across a wetted fabric to disrupt microbial biofilm integrity and weaken electrostatic/cohesive bonds of embedded particles, thereby enabling detachment.

labels.name: Thermoelastic shock disruption
labels.description: Inducing rapid thermal expansion/contraction to generate micro-scale shockwaves that break adhesive bonds between soil and fiber.

labels.name: Electrostatic charge optimization
labels.description: Controlling humidity/surface conditions to maximize charge generation for particle attraction while managing dissipation.

basic.label: Brief low-volume aqueous conditioning
basic.description: Expose fabrics to a small volume of mild, fabric-safe aqueous solution for a short time to loosen soils/biofilms before active disruption.

basic.label: Reduced-volume rinse and low-agitation removal
basic.description: Use focused rinsing, low flow volumes, and limited mechanical agitation after disruption to carry away detached material efficiently.

labels.name: Low-volume localized rinsing
labels.description: Using focused, low-flow fluid application to carry away detached material with minimal water usage.

subordinate.label: Minimal-water PEF washing chamber
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation: a sealed minimal-water chamber with electrodes spanning the fabric, a mild aqueous film, current-limited pulsed electric fields (specified pulse amplitude, duration, frequency), safety interlocks, and electrode geometries tuned for uniform field application to disrupt biofilms and weaken particle bonds.

subordinate.label: Mild fabric-safe aqueous formula and protocol
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation: low-volume solution (near-neutral pH water possibly with low-concentration, fabric-safe surfactant or chelator), brief soak/contact time, controlled volume dosing and distribution to wet fibers without heavy rinsing.

subordinate.label: Low-volume rinse mechanics and flow parameters
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation: targeted rinse jets or recirculating micro-flow, pulsatile flushing, specified reduced water volumes and flow rates, minimal mechanical tumbling, and drain/filtration to remove loosened soils.

idea: A minimal-water washing chamber where clothes are briefly exposed to a mild, fabric-safe aqueous solution. Pulsed electric fields are then applied across the solution and fabric. These pulses disrupt the integrity of microbial biofilms (which encase much of the dirt and odor-causing bacteria) and weaken the electrostatic or cohesive bonds of embedded dirt particles, making them easier to detach and rinse away with significantly less water and agitation.

superordinate.label: Use fluid-substitution and phase behavior to eliminate liquid-surface effects
superordinate.description: Achieve low-water cleaning by substituting water in the garment environment with an alternative fluid and exploiting that fluid's phase transition to remove moisture without surface-tension-driven stresses or extensive wetting.

basic.label: Displace residual water with a transitional fluid and remove moisture via phase change
basic.description: Introduce a non-aqueous or transitional fluid to replace remaining water in textiles, then induce a controlled phase transition (e.g., liquid → supercritical/gas) of that fluid to effect drying and residue-free removal of moisture while avoiding capillary/surface-tension damage.

labels.name: Supercritical fluid cleaning
labels.description: Utilizing fluids at high temp/pressure to act as powerful solvents without detergents.

labels.name: Sublimation-based soil lift
labels.description: Leveraging the rapid phase change of a solid (e.g., CO2) to gas to physically expand and separate soils from fibers.

subordinate.label: Sealed liquid-CO2 (or alternative) system with minimal pre-wash and CO2 phase cycling
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation includes: a sealed chamber for garments; a brief, low-water pre-treatment for stains; injection of liquid CO2 (or another transitional fluid) to displace water; pressurization/heating past CO2's critical point then controlled depressurization to gas for drying; CO2 recovery and recirculation hardware (valves, heat exchangers, condensers); and operating parameters (e.g., CO2 critical point ~31°C and ~73 atm) or alternative fluids/pressures as substitutes.

idea: After a very brief, minimal-water pre-treatment or stain removal, garments are placed in a sealed chamber. Any residual water is replaced with liquid CO2 (or another suitable transitional fluid). The system then takes the CO2 past its critical point, transforming it into a gas. This allows for extremely gentle, residue-free drying without surface tension effects, preventing shrinkage or distortion, and contributing to overall lower water usage by enabling minimal wetting initially.

superordinate.label: Electric-field-driven contaminant removal
superordinate.description: Use of applied electric potentials to mobilize and transport dissolved or suspended contaminants out of textile fibers or pores.

superordinate.label: Minimize bulk fluid by enabling pore-scale flushing
superordinate.description: Replace large-scale convective washing with transport processes that flush contaminants at the pore or fiber scale using a very small fluid volume.

superordinate.label: Local capture and processing of extracted contaminants
superordinate.description: Collect and separate the materials removed from fabric locally so they are not redistributed and can be treated or disposed of separately.

basic.label: Electrokinetic extraction (electro‑osmotic / electrophoretic transport)
basic.description: Applying a potential across fabric immersed in a conductive medium to drive electro-osmotic flow and/or electrophoresis that pulls contaminants out of fibers toward a collection interface.

labels.name: Electrokinetic soil migration
labels.description: Applying an electric field to drive charged soil particles (electrophoresis) out of the textile structure.

basic.label: Low-volume electrolyte immersion
basic.description: Use of a minimal-volume conductive bath (mild electrolyte) that wets fabric sufficiently to support electrokinetic transport without large-scale water exchange or agitation.

labels.name: Fluid-minimizing containment
labels.description: Designing geometries that restrict fluid contact to specific pockets or channels, preventing full immersion.

basic.label: Permeable collection and processing interface
basic.description: A collection electrode, permeable membrane or channel positioned to receive contaminants driven out of the fabric and route them to processing or disposal.

labels.name: Membrane fluid purification
labels.description: Using semi-permeable membranes to separate water from contaminants and cleaning agents for recovery.

labels.name: Carrier regeneration
labels.description: Processes designed to separate collected contaminants from the transport medium to prepare the carrier for reuse.

subordinate.label: Applied potential across fabric in specialized drum
subordinate.description: Concrete implementation: clothes placed in a specialized chamber/drum partially filled with a mild electrolyte; electrodes on opposing sides of the fabric apply a specified voltage/current to induce electro-osmotic flow and electrophoretic motion; design parameters include electrode type, spacing, voltage range, and control of ionic strength.

subordinate.label: Minimal-volume chamber and electrolyte composition
subordinate.description: Concrete implementations: low-volume containment geometry (small immersion layer or targeted wetted zones), choice of mild salts or buffers to achieve conductivity while limiting water use, and mechanical supports to position garments relative to electrodes.

subordinate.label: Collection electrode / permeable membrane and downstream treatment
subordinate.description: Concrete implementations: porous or mesh electrode that accepts expelled fluid, integrated permeable membrane or microchannel that directs collected dirty water to a holding tank, filter, or electrochemical/filtration treatment unit for separation, concentration, and disposal or recycling.

idea: A specialized laundry chamber or drum where clothes are immersed in a very minimal volume of water with a mild electrolyte. An electric potential is applied across the fabric. This induces electro-osmotic flow, drawing dirty water (and dissolved/suspended contaminants) directly out of the fabric pores towards a collection electrode or permeable membrane, effectively "flushing" the fabric internally with minimal bulk water movement or mechanical agitation. The collected dirty water is then processed for disposal or further purification.

superordinate.label: Transfer contaminants into a removable phase
superordinate.description: Achieve cleaning by moving dirt, oils, and odors out of textile fibers into an applied medium that can be separated from the fabric.

superordinate.label: Avoid bulk-liquid rinsing through solid-phase removal
superordinate.description: Replace traditional aqueous wash/rinse cycles with a process that captures soils in a solidifying layer, eliminating the need for large volumes of water.

superordinate.label: maintain fabric compatibility while isolating soils
superordinate.description: Protect textile substrates by using a removal medium and process that do not damage fibers, colors, or finishes while still extracting contaminants.

basic.label: Applied sacrificial adsorptive film
basic.description: A film-forming layer applied onto fabric that selectively adsorbs/entraps contaminants and can be removed intact, carrying captured soils away from the textile.

labels.name: Sacrificial film lift-off
labels.description: Applying a temporary film that entraps surface contaminants as it solidifies and removes them when peeled.

basic.label: Controlled apply–solidify–remove process
basic.description: A sequence of operations (application as mist/thin coat, rapid drying/curing in controlled humidity, and mechanical peel/roll removal) that effects transfer of soils into the film without immersion.

labels.name: Thin-film peel removal
labels.description: Applying a minimal liquid layer to entrap soil, followed by mechanical removal (wiping/peeling) rather than dilution.

basic.label: Formulation and mechanical compatibility
basic.description: Chemistry and mechanical properties chosen to be fabric-safe (nonreactive, non-staining, removable) and tuned to adhere to soils more strongly than to fibers.

labels.name: Biocompatible safety formulation
labels.description: Constraining chemical choices to non-toxic, biodegradable ingredients to allow operation without heavy rinsing.

subordinate.label: Polymer film with adsorptive functional groups
subordinate.description: Concrete instantiation: fabric-safe, dissolvable or semi-solid film-forming polymers (e.g., biodegradable polyesters, water-soluble polyvinyl alcohol variants, or tack-modified polymers) delivered as a fine mist or thin coating; engineered pore/chemistry to bind oils, particulates, and odor molecules; designed to peel as a continuous sheet.

subordinate.label: Application and removal parameters
subordinate.description: Examples: electrostatic or spray mist applicator for thin uniform coating; low-humidity or heated short-cycle drying/curing; peel-off by hand, adhesive-backed roller, or automated stripping mechanism; cycle times and humidity targets tuned to solidify without soaking fibers.

subordinate.label: Safety and selectivity controls
subordinate.description: Examples: low-temperature, non-oxidizing chemistries; controlled film thickness to avoid residue; additives or blockers to prevent dye migration; biodegradability and disposal guidelines for contaminated film waste.

idea: A laundry system where a fine, fabric-safe, dissolvable or semi-solid film-forming polymer solution is applied to the garment as a mist or thin coating. This film is engineered with adsorptive properties for dirt, oils, and odors. After a short drying/curing time in a low-humidity environment, the film solidifies, encapsulating the contaminants. It is then gently peeled off the garment by hand or an automated roller, carrying the accumulated dirt away, leaving clean fabric without water rinsing.

superordinate.label: Feedback-driven resource minimization
superordinate.description: Use of sensing and control to adapt cleaning intensity so resources (water) are used only when contamination is detected.

superordinate.label: Alternative low-water cleaning modality
superordinate.description: Replace or supplement bulk-water washing with physical or chemical cleaning methods that use little or no water.

superordinate.label: Signal-mediated user/system decision
superordinate.description: Conveying a clear signal when additional cleaning is required so the system or user escalates to a more intensive process only when necessary.

basic.label: Biochemical/optical residue reporter as sensor
basic.description: A chemical or biological indicator that produces a detectable optical signal (bioluminescence) in the presence of organic residues, providing direct evidence of insufficient cleaning.

labels.name: Optical residue detection
labels.description: Using sensors to identify specific locations of remaining organic residue for targeted cleaning.

basic.label: Minimal-water cleaning process
basic.description: A cleaning step that removes soil with very little water (e.g., misting, plasma, steam, ultrasonic) used as the default/first-pass treatment.

basic.label: Control logic for conditional escalation
basic.description: Decision rules and interfaces that interpret the sensor signal and trigger notifications or automated deeper-clean cycles only when residue is detected.

labels.name: Adaptive process control
labels.description: Systems that detect fabric/soil properties and adjust energy inputs to optimize cleaning while preventing damage.

subordinate.label: Bioluminescent agent + optical readout
subordinate.description: Specific implementations such as fabric-safe luciferase/luciferin systems or enzyme-triggered fluorogenic probes, methods of application (brief spray, embedded microcapsules, or activation), and photodetectors/cameras + threshold algorithms to read emitted light.

subordinate.label: Examples of low-water methods
subordinate.description: Concrete techniques like fine misting cycles, cold plasma pulses, steam bursts, or ultrasonic agitation integrated into appliance chambers or garment cabinets.

subordinate.label: Practical control & user notification mechanisms
subordinate.description: Firmware/software implementations: emission thresholds, automatic re-run profiles (longer wash, full-water cycle), mobile/app or panel alerts, and logging for user choice or automated action.

idea: Integrate a bioluminescent detection system into a laundry appliance or garment cabinet. After a minimal-water cleaning cycle (e.g., misting, plasma), a mild, fabric-safe bioluminescent agent is briefly applied or activated. If significant organic residues (like bacteria, body oils) remain, they trigger a light emission, indicating the need for further cleaning or a more intensive approach. This smart feedback loop ensures that clothes are only cleaned as much as necessary, significantly reducing unnecessary water consumption.

superordinate.label: Precision identification and localization of contaminants
superordinate.description: Detect and map the spatial distribution of dirt/stains at micro-scale so cleaning actions are applied only where needed.

superordinate.label: Localized non-chemical physical removal via directed energy

idea: A sealed garment cabinet that generates a fine, electrostatically charged mist of ultra-pure water (or a mild cleaning solution). These charged nano-droplets are engineered to act as "dirt nuclei," preferentially attracting and encapsulating fine particulate dirt, lint, and odor molecules from the garments via electrostatic forces and targeted surface chemistry. Once sufficiently agglomerated and weighted with contaminants, a controlled electrostatic field or gentle air current causes these dirt-laden droplets to coalesce and precipitate onto a collection surface at the bottom of the chamber, effectively "raining" the dirt out of the fabric without wetting the garment or requiring mechanical action.

idea: A garment refreshing cabinet with internal curved surfaces and precisely angled air nozzles designed to exploit the Coandă effect. A continuous, laminar sheet of high-velocity air is generated and directed to flow smoothly over the garments. This non-turbulent, wall-attached airflow creates a gentle, continuous shear force across the fabric surfaces, effectively lifting and carrying away dry dust, lint, pet hair, and superficial particulate matter without harsh mechanical contact. The dirt-laden air is then silently directed into a high-efficiency filter system, providing a very gentle, water-free cleaning and deodorizing method.

idea: A controlled environment cabinet or low-humidity wash chamber that applies a fine, fabric-safe mist containing targeted fungal enzymes or specific fungal spore extracts. These enzymes, under optimized temperature and humidity conditions, specifically target and degrade stubborn organic stains (e.g., grass, wine, oil) and complex odor-causing compounds embedded in fabric. This breaks the stains down into smaller, water-soluble, or volatile molecules that are easily wiped away or dissipated by gentle airflow, significantly reducing the need for bulk water washing and harsh chemicals for tough stains.

idea: A dry-cleaning appliance featuring rollers made from a "smart" biomimetic polymer whose surface exhibits tunable, reversible bio-adhesion. As garments pass through, a mild, fabric-safe stimulus (e.g., a specific light wavelength, slight pH change, or mild electric field) activates the roller's surface to temporarily increase its adhesion, causing it to pick up a broad range of dirt, oils, and particulate matter from the fabric. A different stimulus then instantly reduces the adhesion, causing the collected dirt to release cleanly from the roller into a waste receptacle, making the roller self-cleaning and reusable for continuous, water-free garment cleaning.

idea: A garment refreshing cabinet with internal surfaces coated with or containing encapsulated, fabric-safe quantum dots. The cabinet is equipped with specific light sources (e.g., visible LED light). When illuminated, the quantum dots efficiently generate highly reactive species that break down odor molecules, volatile organic compounds, and light organic soiling directly on the fabric surface. This provides a dry, chemical-free, and water-free method for refreshing garments, potentially using lower energy light sources and offering superior catalytic efficiency compared to traditional photocatalysts like TiO2.
